"I wouldn't need it for long," Darb added quickly.
"I'd be happy to bring it back to Laddno campaign headquarters tomorrow to discuss how I can help the cause."
The man still looked hesitant. But finally he smiled. "I suppose that would be all right."
Soon the deflated boat was draped over Darb's shoulders. The kids hurried toward the tree.
"What was that all about?" Zann asked.
Darb smiled slyly. "We're going to Skellia, right? A drowning world with weak magic?
I thought a boat that doesn't require magic might come in handy."
"Good thinking, Darb!" Perda said. "Now we won't have to use magic to create a raft."
"And that means we won't attract the gulpers." Zann shivered, thinking of the magic-eating creatures that swam in Skellia's waters.
When Zann and his friends approached the tree, the wormhole spun open.
"I was hoping the wormhole had disappeared," Gliss joked weakly.
"Not this one," Zann said. "It's been here for a long time."
Perda laughed. "Hey, maybe the Source is located right here under this spooky old tree with its super powerful wormhole!"
"Who knows?" Zann snapped his fingers. A Shackle spell linked the friends' hands together.
Zann stepped toward the wormhole. "Let's go!"
Zann felt dizzy as he and his friends tumbled through the vortex.
Lights flashed and strange worlds passed by.
Slowly he reached into his pocket and pulled out the guidelink.
"Give me that!" Perda called over the whooshing sound of the vortex.
"I think I can make it work."
"I hope you're right!" Zann placed the device in her hand.
He wished he'd paid more attention when his parents were explaining the device's abilities.
Perda fiddled with the guidelink.
"What are you doing?" Gliss asked her.
"I'm supposed to rub it to create friction," Perda said.
"Then I focus on what type of magic I want it to find.
It should pull us toward any world nearby that matches my thoughts."
She frowned. "But so far nothing is happening!"
"You have to figure it out!" Gliss sounded frantic.
"Otherwise we could end up flying through the vortex forever!"
Suddenly Perda swerved toward one of the wormholes, dragging her friends with her.
Zann grabbed the wormhole’s edge. Instantly the wormhole pulled them in and spat them out on the other side.
Zann held his breath, expecting to splash into the stormy waters of Skellia.
Instead he landed on wet ground. "Oof!" he blurted out.
Gliss sat up and rubbed her head. "Ouch," she said.
Then she looked around. "Hey, this isn't Skellia."
"Not unless the oceans disappeared since we were here," Darb said.
The world they'd landed in looked similar to Magica.
They were in a forest clearing, with tall trees shading the light of a bright orange sun.
Birds swooped overhead, and an insect buzzed in the grass nearby.
"Oh well." Perda sighed. "I guess I'm still figuring out how the guidelink works."
"At least this world looks nice and peaceful." Gliss peered around.
Then she wrinkled her nose and looked down.
"It's kind of soggy right here though.
Let's find a drier spot to rest and regain our energy."
Zann nodded. It took a lot of energy just to stay conscious in the vortex.
They usually had to rest before they could travel again.
"Wait! Don't go anywhere yet," Darb said.
"We need to pay attention to landmarks so we can return to the wormhole when we're ready."
"Oops. Good point," Zann said. As usual, the wormhole had spun shut as soon as they'd moved away from it.
Now it was only visible as a tiny ripple in the air.
If Zann hadn't known it was there, he wouldn't even have noticed it.
"I see a crooked tree over there, and some blue flowers," Gliss said.
"Good," Perda said. "We'll definitely be able to spot that tree again.
Now let's go uphill. It should be dry there."
She led the way up a gentle slope.
Soon they reached a sunny clearing. Zann flopped onto the dry ground and looked at Perda.
"So why didn't the guidelink work?" he asked.
She shrugged and sat down beside him.
"I think I know what I did wrong," she said.
"I was focusing on the gulpers from Skellia, since they probably have the most magic on that world.
But when Gliss said the thing about flying through the vortex, I thought about birds."
Darb watched a bright purple bird land nearby and peck at some yellow flowers.
"There definitely are a lot of birds here," he said.
"Maybe they're the source of this world's magic."
"They could be," Zann agreed. Then he frowned.
"Uh-oh. Do you think our magic will work here?"
"I hope so, or we won't be able to open the wormhole!" Gliss' eyes widened.
"We'd better test it. I'll conjure us something to drink."
She snapped her fingers. Blink!
Zann felt a sudden surge of magic energy.
At the same time, the entire landscape around them changed!
The sunny meadow had disappeared. They were now sitting in the shade of several large trees.
A small flock of multicolored birds perched on a squat shrub with shiny blue leaves.
Zann gasped and jumped to his feet.
"What happened? Did we accidentally zap somewhere else?"
"I don't think so." Darb looked around.
"We're still on a hill. And the position of the sun hasn't changed.
I think we're in the same exact spot."
"But everything around us looks different!" Perda said. "The trees, the birds . . ."
"That must be how magic works in this world," Darb said.
"Gliss' magic friction changed the landscape around us."
"Yeah." Zann gulped. "I wonder if it made that crooked tree move around too.
We might not be able to find the wormhole without it."
"Oh no," Gliss said. "What about the wormhole itself?
What if it moved? What if it's gone?"
Perda held up the guidelink. "This is supposed to be able to locate strong sources of magic, right?
Maybe it can lead us back to the wormhole."
"Do you know how to make it do that?" Darb asked.
"No." Perda bit her lip. "But I'll figure it out."
She rubbed the guidelink. Blink!
The landscape changed again. Now the kids found themselves standing among bushes with spiky leaves.
Nearby several large, six-legged creatures with shaggy fur sniffed around in the grass.
"Hmm," Perda said. She rubbed the guidelink again. Blink!
Now a deep, tangled forest surrounded the kids.
Blink!
Again the scenery changed. Now the open meadow was back.
But instead of birds, there was a swarm of large insects buzzing around a tree with purple bark.
"Stop!" Gliss grabbed the guidelink out of Perda's hand.
"Every time you create friction, the landscape changes!"
"Sorry." Perda looked nervous.
Zann knew how she felt. It seemed like they couldn't use magic in this world at all—not without getting lost.
So how were they going to find their way back to the wormhole?
While Zann, Perda, and Gliss were beginning to panic, Darb appeared calm.
"Don't worry," he said. "I think I can get us back to the wormhole."
"How?" Gliss cried. "We can't use magic!"
Darb smiled. "I can't ever use magic. I'm used to living without it. Give me a minute."
He squinted up toward the sun and then glanced around.
"What's he doing?" Perda whispered.
Zann shrugged. "Let's wait and see."
Darb looked up again. Then he closed his eyes and just stood there for a moment.
"Okay," he said at last. "I think it's this way."
Zann and the girls followed as Darb led the way.
After a moment Darb paused. He looked around and then closed his eyes again.
When he opened them, he made a turn and then walked some more.
"I think he's using his non-magical senses to try to find his way back to the wormhole," Zann told the others softly.
"That's right," Darb said.
"The sun was just above our left shoulders when we were walking up the hill, so now I'm trying to keep it just to our right."
Within minutes Zann spotted a slight shimmer in the air up ahead.
"The wormhole!" he shouted. "There it is!"
"Whew!" Gliss sounded relieved. "We're lucky you found it, Darb. Our landmarks are nowhere in sight!"
Zann nodded. The scenery looked very different than it had when they'd arrived.
But he didn't really care about that anymore.
"Let's get out of here," he said.
"Are you sure we've rested enough?" Gliss asked.
"No," Perda said. "But I agree with Zann. We need to get to Skellia and help Ello."
They shackled themselves together and dived into the wormhole.
Almost immediately Zann realized they should have rested for longer. He felt weak.
He and his friends careened wildly around.
"This is terrible!" Gliss shouted. "We have to find a place to rest."
"Just grab the first world we pass," Darb called out.
"No!" Perda cried. "What if we end up back in Fardark?"
"No way that's happening!" Zann declared. Fardark was a creepy world full of horrible creatures, like scatter beasts.
Perda was right—they couldn't risk landing somewhere like that. But they had to stop soon.
"Give me that," he blurted out. He grabbed the guidelink from Perda.
With the last of his energy, he focused on soothing, intelligent magic.
A second later he felt the device tugging him toward an upcoming wormhole.
Moments later they tumbled out into another world.
This one looked similar to Magica too. But it smelled completely different.
"Ugh!" Gliss held her nose. "It's Niffia!"
Zann grabbed his own nose. He'd recognize Niffia anywhere.
It was the stinkiest world he'd ever smelled!
"I wish we could try again." Perda glanced at the wormhole.
"But I think we'll have to make the best of it until we're rested."
"At least the people in this world are friendly." Darb pointed. "Look, here come some Niffians now."
The Niffians smiled brightly. "Welcome back, my young friends!" the leader said.
"We're so happy that you've chosen to return to our beautiful world."
Zann forced a smile. He'd stopped holding his nose when the Niffians had arrived.
"Thank you," he said. "We needed a nice place to rest and restore our energy."
"You've come to the right world," another Niffian said, beaming.
"Please come with us and share some food and drink."
The kids followed the Niffians to the nearest town.
As they ate, Zann and his friends told the Niffians about their adventures since their last visit to Niffia.
When Zann mentioned Wyssa, the Niffians looked more delighted than ever.
"Ah, Wyssa!" one of them cried. "How is our most esteemed friend?"
"We're not sure." Zann traded a look with his friends.
During their first visit to Niffia, they'd been surprised to find out how much the Niffians liked Wyssa.
She'd never seemed very friendly to Zann or the others.
"We haven't seen her since she left Magica with Morb," Perda said.
"Morb." One of the Niffians frowned slightly.
"Ah, yes. I believe that was the name of her, um, companion during her most recent visit."
Zann was surprised. "Wyssa brought Morb here?"
"Only briefly," another Niffian said. He and the others suddenly looked much more solemn than usual.
"She stopped only long enough to collect a bit of pupu leaf."
"Pupu leaf?" Perda echoed. "What's that for?"
The Niffians exchanged glances. "We didn't ask why she needed it," one said.
"However," another added, "the pupu is mostly used for spells involving immobilization."
Zann shuddered as he remembered Wyssa's threat to feed Morb to a scatter beast.
Was that why she'd needed the pupu? To immobilize him long enough for the fearsome creature to find him?
"So," the Niffian leader said. "Why are you four traveling through the vortex again?"
Zann told the Niffians about their current mission to find Skellia and help Ello.
"We'll fetch you some oogberry," one Niffian said, while another rushed off toward the forest.
"That's an important ingredient in searching spells."
"Just relax for now though." The Niffian leader smiled. "We'll take care of everything."
For the next hour, Zann did his best to rest and ignore the stink.
He and his friends were talking about Niffia when Zann's head exploded in pain. Clutching his forehead, he groaned.
"Zann!" Perda cried.
Zann hardly heard her. He fell to the floor, landing on the guidelink.
Ello's frightened face appeared in his mind.
"Help!" Ello wailed. "Please, hurry!"
Zann grabbed the guidelink. "We're coming!" he cried, even though he knew Ello couldn't hear him.
Or could he? Immediately Ello's face brightened.
"Hurry!" he said again, before fading away.
Laddno frowned as a female member of the Red Council droned on about election details.
The businessman had wandered to the back of the room ten minutes earlier.
He glanced toward the group. Boz was sitting up front with his non-Red daughter and her husband.
All three were listening carefully to what the Red Council member was saying.
Laddno glared at Boz, but the old Magic Master didn't even look his way.
Laddno began pacing. He didn't like being ignored, especially by a bunch of snooty Reds and their cronies.
But that would all change soon. Once he was elected king, Laddno planned to make some big changes.
He'd start by hanging an enormous portrait of himself in the palace.
Then no one could ignore him—or his power!
He was thinking about what color to paint the throne room when the familiar pain filled his head again.
He held his head and staggered out of the room.
He collapsed against the wall, panting as the pain subsided slightly.
The voice in his head spoke.
"What?" Laddno replied. "How soon?"
He paused and listened again. Then he frowned.
"Are you sure they're really coming?" Laddno asked. "What if they can't do it?"
Once again he fell silent as the voice raged on. Finally Laddno nodded.
"All right," he said resolutely. "I'll begin immediately."
"Hold still," a Niffian said as he dabbed purple goo on Zann's fingers.
Perda stared at her own fingers, which were already coated with the stuff.
"How does this work again?" she asked.
"This oogberry paste will work with your magical friction," the Niffian explained.
"All you need to do is think of the place you wish to visit.
When the paste glows, it means you're near your destination."
"That sounds sort of like the guidelink."
Gliss glanced at the device sticking out of Zann's pocket.
"With that, we need to think about a certain type of magic."
The Niffian smiled. "With the paste, you just need to think of a person or place."
"That will make things easier," Zann said.
He looked at his hands. "Okay, I think we're ready."
He was grateful to the Niffians for helping them.
But he was eager to get away from their stinky world as soon as possible. Besides, he was worried about Ello.
Soon Zann and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Think about Skellia, everyone!" Perda called.
Within seconds the paste began to glow.
Zann spotted an approaching wormhole. "That must be Skellia up ahead!" he shouted.
Moments later they plunged through the wormhole and into cold water.
The water was so rough, Zann was glad that the Shackle spell was holding them all together.
Suddenly something large glided past beneath them.
"A gulper!" Perda yelled. "Quick, inflate the boat!"
Darb spit out a mouthful of water.
Then he pulled down the boat, which had been draped over his shoulders, and yanked the little tab.
Soon the boat was bobbing on the waves. By now the gulper had moved away.
Zann was relieved. Since they hadn't used magic, the creature hadn't been interested in them.
When they were all on the boat, Zann collapsed and caught his breath. "We did it," he said.
"Thanks to the Niffians." Perda looked at her hand. "My oogberry paste washed off."
"Mine too," Gliss said.
Zann saw that his fingers had also returned to their normal color.
"Oh well. Hopefully the guidelink will help us find our way back to Magica."
"First we have to find Ello," Darb said.
Zann sat up and looked around. From horizon to horizon, all he could see were churning gray waves.
There was no sign of land anywhere.
Gliss peered at her hand. "Maybe there's some oogberry paste stuck under our fingernails."
"I have a better idea," Perda said. "Let's use the guidelink.
Since it tracks magic, we might be able to find Ello with it.
We just need to focus on whatever type of magic Ello is using to communicate with Zann."
Gliss frowned. "But we don't know what type that is."
"It's worth a try," Zann said.
He rubbed the guidelink and focused on Ello.
He thought about the magic that Ello had used during their last visit to Skellia.
At first nothing happened. So Perda and Gliss put their hands on the guidelink too and added their own thoughts to Zann's.
Finally something tugged on the boat.
"I think it's working!" Perda cried.
The boat floated along, pulled by the guidelink's magic.
Suddenly a gulper rose out of the water!
"Oh, no!" Gliss wailed. "The guidelink attracted a gulper!"
"Everyone, stop using magic," Darb called out.
"Let's just sit here until the gulper swims away."
When the gulper was gone, they tried again.
Two more gulpers appeared, drawn by the energy of the guidelink.
"What are we going to do?" Gliss said. "This isn't working!"
"Let's try once more," Perda suggested. "This time, don't focus on Ello. Just think about finding the strongest magic source around."
She looked at Zann. "Your parents said it could do that, right?"
"I think so," Zann said. "Let's try it."
This time the guidelink responded almost immediately. The boat sped over the waves.
"Whoa!" Perda cried.
"Wow," Darb said. "The guidelink must have found a really strong power source!"
"Yeah," Zann said slowly. "That's weird though. I thought Skellia didn't have much native magic."
"Look!" Perda shouted. "It's another boat."
Zann peered through the sea spray. Something was bobbing on the waves up ahead.
When they got closer, he laughed with relief.
It was a rickety houseboat with a small figure waving to them from the deck.
"It's Ello!" he cried. "We found him!"
"You came!" Ello cried as the inflatable boat bumped against the houseboat. "I thought you wouldn't!"
"Of course we came," Zann said. He was happy to finally see Ello's face in person. "Help us up."
Ello held out his hand. Everyone climbed up onto the houseboat's deck, and then Zann and Darb pulled up the inflatable boat.
Gliss turned to smile at Ello.
"We're glad you're safe!" she cried, flinging her arms around him.
"Hey!" Ello shook off her hug and took a quick step back.
Perda frowned at him. "What's wrong?"
"Nothing," Ello said quickly. "Uh, I'm sorry. I've been alone so long.
I guess I've forgotten how to act around people."
Zann glanced around. "Wow, this houseboat is bigger than it looked from a distance."
He bent to peer at an odd stain on the floor.
The boat was missing a few chunks of wood here and there too.
But for the most part, the vessel seemed sturdy.
"Why are you alone?" Gliss asked Ello. "What happened to your people?"
Ello scratched his head. He was wearing a pair of dark gloves.
That seemed a little odd to Zann, but he soon forgot about it.
There were more important questions to be answered.
"Wyssa said she was going to come back and rescue you," Zann said. "Didn't she do that?"
Ello frowned. "She did come back to Skellia.
She promised to take all of them—uh, I mean us—to an unoccupied world where we could resettle.
But when they left, I was at the back of the group. They accidentally left me behind."
Gliss gasped. "That's horrible! Didn't she come back for you?"
Zann was wondering the same thing. Wyssa might be kind of cranky and unpredictable, but she had very strong magical powers.
She could have easily come back and rescued Ello once she realized he was missing.
"Obviously not." Ello frowned, looking around the houseboat.
"I figured a gulper must have eaten all the wormholes after they left.
Or maybe she just didn't bother to come back for me."
He shrugged. "Wyssa probably had other things on her mind besides helping me."
Ello sounded bitter. Zann was surprised.
The last time Zann had met Ello, the Skellian boy was kind and optimistic despite his people's dire situation.
But Ello had been alone for a long time now.
He'd been left behind and apparently forgotten.
Anyone in his situation would be bitter.
Darb was peering through a door leading to the interior of the houseboat.
"This place is pretty nice," he said. "Where did it come from?"
"Where did what come from?" Ello fiddled with the tips of one glove, not looking at Zann or his friends.
"The houseboat," Perda said. She sounded impatient. "Where did you get this houseboat?"
"I made it, of course," Ello said.
"Really?" Darb stared at him in surprise.
Zann and the girls walked over to Darb and looked through the door too.
The interior room contained a bed, a table, and various other necessities.
"But your people don't have much magic," Gliss blurted out.
"How in the world did you make all this stuff?"
"Yeah," Zann said. "Uh, no offense. But last time we met, you could barely conjure food or water.
So how did you manage to conjure this boat all by yourself?"
Ello looked away from them and bit his lip.
"Um . . . I'll tell you about it later, okay?
Right now we have to get out of here.
A storm is coming, and my boat just sprang a leak this morning. See?"
He knelt down and placed his gloved palm on the deck.
At that moment Zann was distracted by the guidelink, which jumped in his pocket.
He glanced down and wondered what had set it off.
Then he noticed a gulper glide by.
Perhaps that creature's magic had caused the guidelink to jump?
He turned his attention back to Ello. Ello had just stood up again.
In the spot he'd touched, water was welling up through a crack in the boards.
"Yikes!" Perda stared at the leak. "I didn't see that at first.
You're right—we need to get out of here."
"Especially if Ello’s correct and there's going to be a storm." Darb squinted up at the sky.
Zann looked up too. As usual on Skellia, the sky was filled with foreboding clouds, though the sun was peeking through in a few spots.
It didn't look particularly stormy to Zann.
But he assumed Ello knew the weather on Skellia much better than he did.
"Okay, let's take our boat," he said.
"We can use the guidelink to find a wormhole."
"The what?" Ello sounded curious.
While Darb and the girls tossed the boat back into the sea, Zann quickly told Ello about the guidelink.
"Its power will attract gulpers," Zann said.
"But if we're quick, we can get through a wormhole before they catch up."
By then the other three kids were already in the boat. "Hurry up!" Perda called.
"Coming!" Zann jumped into the smaller boat.
Then he looked up. "Come on, Ello!"
Ello hesitated, looking fearful as he stared down at them.
"Hurry!" Gliss cried.
Finally Ello jumped off the deck. Just then a large wave pushed the small boat away.
Ello let out a cry as he plunged into the sea between the two vessels.
"Oops," Zann said. "Get ready to help him aboard when he surfaces."
He leaned over the side, ready to grab Ello's hand.
But when Ello's head finally popped into view, he was too far away.
"Swim this way!" Perda called.
Ello's arms flailed. He gurgled and sank underwater again.
"Oh no!" Gliss cried. "I think he's drowning!"
"I'm coming, Ello!" Perda cried. She dived into the water.
Zann plunged into the chilly sea too.
He dived down into the murky water and spotted Perda just below him.
When he reached her, she had Ello by the arm.
Zann grabbed Ello's other arm and helped Perda drag him back to the surface. Ello coughed and spit out water.
"Over here!" Gliss called.
She and Darb reached out to pull Ello aboard.
Then they helped Zann and Perda as well.
"Whew! That was close," Perda said breathlessly.
"What happened?" Darb asked Ello. "Can't you swim?"
"Of course I can." Ello was shaking.
"I suppose I must be weak from my long solitude.
Let's find a wormhole and get out of here."
"Okay." Zann pulled out the guidelink and handed it to Perda. "How should we do this?"
Perda rubbed the device. "Think about wormholes, everyone," she said.
"Or the vortex. Either one might work."
Several gulpers surfaced nearby. Then there was a tug on the guidelink.
"This way," Perda said. She held on tightly as the device pulled the boat along. The gulpers followed.
Darb eyed the gulpers. "I hope the guidelink helps us get to the wormhole first.
Otherwise all it's doing is helping those things find a snack."
"Maybe we should all hold the guidelink," Gliss suggested.
Everyone put a hand on the device. Zann glanced at Ello's hand.
"Ello, it might work better if you take off your gloves," he said.
Before Ello could respond, the boat rocketed forward.
The guidelink vibrated under their hands. The gulpers were soon far behind.
Perda pointed ahead. "There's a wormhole!"
Zann nodded. "Get ready to jump, everyone!"
"What about the boat?" Darb said.
"We'll have to leave it behind." Zann glanced over his shoulder and saw that the gulpers were gaining on them. "There's no time to deflate it."
Darb nodded, but he looked uneasy.
Perda performed a Shackle spell. With everyone shackled together, Zann got ready for the leap into the wormhole.
"Now!" Zann cried.
Everyone jumped. Whoosh! A moment later they were spinning through the vortex again.
"We did it!" Gliss exclaimed. "I've never been so happy to be in this crazy place."
Perda laughed. "I know what you mean."
She glanced at Ello, who was shackled between her and Zann. "Welcome to the vortex, Ello."
"What?" Ello looked around. "Oh, right. This is my first time in the vortex."
"That's weird," Zann thought. Ello sounded flat and unimpressed.
Usually people were freaked out during their first time in the vortex.
"Let's see if we can find your people," Zann said.
"Did Wyssa tell you anything about the world where she was bringing them?
If we know what type of magic it has, maybe we can use the guidelink to find it."
"I have no idea," Ello said. "Wyssa didn't tell us anything.
Maybe I should just come back to Magica with you. I've always wanted to visit."
Gliss raised an eyebrow. "Don't you want to find your family?"
"I'm sure you know some powerful people in Magica who can help me get home," Ello said.
Zann was surprised. When his parents were lost in the vortex, Zann wanted more than anything to be reunited with them.
But Ello didn't seem to be in much of a hurry to find his own family.
Perda gave Ello a suspicious look. "Why wouldn't Wyssa tell your people where she was taking them?"
"She might have been distracted by Morb," Gliss suggested before Ello could respond.
"Maybe she was still trying to figure out what to do with Morb."
"That's it!" Ello said quickly. "She did seem distracted. And Morb kept trying to escape.
That's probably why she didn't tell us anything."
"She brought Morb with her to Skellia?" Zann was surprised again. "Why would she do that?"
"And didn't your people ask any questions?" Perda persisted. "Your mother or Rellu weren't curious?"
"Who?" Ello said.
Zann stared at him. "Rellu," he repeated. "The elder from your village."
"Oh, him." Ello cleared his throat. "Of course. I, uh, didn't hear you."
Zann couldn't ignore his uneasy feelings anymore. Something about Ello was odd.
And judging by the suspicious look on her face, Perda felt the same way.
Perda gestured to an approaching wormhole. "Let's exit here. I think we need to have a talk."
Zann grabbed the edge of the wormhole, peeking through to make sure it didn't look like Fardark or any other unpleasant world.
The landscape was covered in ice and snow, but otherwise didn't seem dangerous.
When they'd landed in the soft snow, Perda dissolved the shackles.
"Brr!" Gliss said. She snapped her fingers to conjure a warm coat.
"Hey, our magic seems to work here."
Perda was staring at Ello. "So, Ello, tell us again exactly how you got left behind."
"And where that houseboat came from," Zann added.
Ello frowned. "Why are you interrogating me?" he whined.
"I just want to get back to the safety of Magica."
"But you've never even been to Magica," Perda said.
"Why don't you want to find your family instead?"
"Yeah," Gliss said. "That does seem weird."
Ello scowled. "Fine," he said. "You want answers? Here you go!" He snapped his fingers.
Ello's familiar face began to change appearance.
Zann watched with confusion. Then he gasped. Ello's face was gone.
In its place was a different, even more familiar one.
"Morb!" Zann cried.
Perda's eyes widened. "You used a Masking spell!"
"Clever girl." Morb glared at the kids.
"All of you really are too clever for your own good."
Before the kids could react, he plucked the guidelink out of Perda's hand.
With a triumphant cackle, he disappeared through the wormhole.
Zann and his friends stood silently for a moment. Perda was the first to speak.
"We just rescued Morb!" she cried.
"But how is he even still alive?" Darb blurted out. "Wyssa said . . ."
"And how did he get enough magic to send Zann those messages?" Gliss said.
"Or do that Masking spell? Or even make the houseboat?"
"Never mind all that," Zann said. "We have to get back to Magica and warn everyone!"
"How?" Gliss glanced toward the wormhole. "We don't have the guidelink to help us anymore."
Zann realized she was right. He gulped. Still, they had no choice.
"We'll get home," he said, trying to sound confident.
"Now let's get out of here. This world is freezing."
They shackled themselves together and returned to the vortex.
"Now what?" Darb asked.
"Let's just check every wormhole we pass," Perda said. "We have to pass Magica eventually."
Each time they passed a wormhole, they grabbed the edge and looked in.
First they saw a world with grass taller than their heads.
Another world had three white suns shining over pale yellow trees.
The next wormhole revealed a world with thick purple fog.
Finally they reached a wormhole with a view of a beautiful spired city.
"That looks like Pax," Perda said.
Zann remembered the pleasant world they'd visited before.
"Let's stop here for a while. We can regain our strength before continuing."
Pax was just as nice as Zann remembered, but it was hard to enjoy it when they were so anxious about finding their way home.
As soon as they'd rested enough, the group returned to the vortex.
After that, Zann lost track of how many worlds they passed. But none of them was Magica.
When they came to another world they recognized, called Gabble, they stopped to rest again. Then they continued on.
More worlds followed—worlds with blue suns, polka-dotted trees, odd-looking creatures. None looked anything like Magica.
Zann felt his magical energy faltering again.
"We need to stop for another rest," he said. "Here's a wormhole—" He froze with fear.
"It's Fardark!" Perda cried.
Zann pushed himself away from the wormhole, and again everyone tumbled through the vortex.
"We definitely don't want to stop there," he said. "We'll try the next world."
But they recognized the next world too.
"Ugh," Gliss said. "It's that weird place where nasty dragons are in charge."
"Drac," Darb added. "We can't stop here either."
"Okay." Zann felt exhausted. "We can't go much longer without a rest though."
The next wormhole revealed a bustling city.
People hurried along, carrying shopping bags or talking with friends.
A trio of small boys kicked a ball in the street.
"This one looks okay." Perda sounded tired.
Zann started to pull himself through.
"No!" Darb cried. "It's the no-magic world! Remember our last stop here?
We won't be able to open the wormhole once it closes."
Zann looked more closely, wondering how Darb had recognized it.
"How do you know it's the no-magic world?"
Darb pointed. "That black-and-white ball. It's just like the one we saw last time."
Zann hesitated. The ball did look the same.
But lots of objects ended up traveling from one world to another.
"We can't risk it," Gliss said.
Zann knew his friends were right. "Okay, let's keep going.
But whatever world we come to next, we're going to have to stop. No matter what."
When the next wormhole came into view, Zann took a deep breath and pulled himself and his friends through.
They landed on a gnarly tree root.
Zann sat up and looked around. When he spotted several tiny houses, he felt a surge of hope.
"We're in Rood!" Gliss cried. "Hooray!"
Zann's friends talked excitedly. But Zann was too relieved to speak.
Rood had once been known as World X.
It was the only world where the outgoing wormholes led directly into other worlds, bypassing the vortex entirely.
Morb had come here to try to destroy Magica, but Zann and his friends had stopped him.
"We got lucky," Darb said.
Perda nodded. "All we have to do is find the queen of Rood.
She can find a wormhole back to Magica!
Then we can warn everyone about Morb!"
A short while later, the kids stood before the tiny Queen of Rood.
"I'm so glad your travels brought you back to Rood," the queen said.
"I've been hoping to thank you again for ridding my peaceful world of Morb's evil influence."
Zann looked down and so did his friends.
Nobody wanted to tell the queen that they'd just accidentally released Morb!
"Um, thanks," Zann said. "We were happy to do it."
The queen smiled up at them as she summoned a wormhole with a wave of her hand.
She waved again, and the wormhole spun open.
"This wormhole will take you directly into the palace in First City," the queen said.
"Really?" Perda exclaimed. "But last time we were here, you told us you can't summon individual wormholes."
"Your friend Wyssa stopped by with a potion," the queen said.
Zann and his friends thanked the queen and then stepped through the wormhole.
They emerged into a shadowy corner of the palace throne room.
The scene there was chaotic. People hurried back and forth, shouting frantically.
For a second Zann wasn't sure what was happening.
He spotted his parents and Boz. Near them were Venna, Teplo, and Gliss' uncle, Gar.
"This is an outrage!" Boz shouted. He hadn't noticed the kids in the corner.
Zann gasped as he realized his grandfather was immobilized by magical shackles. So were his parents and Teplo.
"I'm sorry, sir." A palace guard stepped toward the shackled adults. Several other guards followed.
"We're going to have to lock the four of you in the dungeon until we get to the bottom of things."
"Listen to me!" Venna shouted.
But nobody was listening to her. The guards dragged the prisoners away.
Zann started to rush forward, but Darb held him back.
"Let them go," he whispered. "Otherwise the guards might grab you too."
Zann sighed. He knew Darb was right.
The guards had already taken his family away.
There was nothing he could do right now.
Laddno strode to the middle of the room.
He whistled for attention, making the sound even louder with a Swelling spell.
Everyone stopped talking and turned to stare at him.
"Don't panic!" he shouted. "I'll get to the bottom of what's happening here, believe me."
"Why should we believe you?" Venna snapped.
"This is probably your fault. Everyone knows you're anti-Red."
"That's not true." Laddno puffed out his chest.
"I care about all of Magica's citizens. That's why I want to lead Magica."
Laddno snapped his fingers and zapped out of sight.
As soon as the businessman was gone, Zann broke free of Darb's grasp. He rushed toward Venna.
"What's going on?" he cried. "Why did those guards take away my parents, Boz, and Teplo?"
"Zann? What are you doing here?" Venna sounded surprised, and a little shaken.
"Where did you kids come from? Never mind—it doesn't matter." She sighed.
"Your parents and Boz were accused of stealing several important items from their lab.
They're being held in the dungeon while the guards search their homes.
Teplo tried to stop the arrest, so he's being held too."
Zann gulped, immediately thinking about the guidelink.
"Why are my parents being accused of stealing?" he blurted out.
"I mean, it could have been anyone."
Perda shot him a worried look. Zann guessed that all of his friends were thinking the same thing he was.
This was all their fault! They had taken the guidelink, but Zann's family was in trouble for it.
And the kids couldn't even give it back now, since Morb had taken it!
"Yeah, who accused Zann's parents and Boz?" Perda put in.
"There's no way to prove they took that thing."
"What thing?" Venna looked confused.
"The guidelink!" Gliss cried. "Zann's parents didn't steal it!"
"What's a guidelink?" Venna shook her head. "Never mind, I don't care.
Whatever it might be, the other items that are missing are much more important."
"Huh?" Now Zann was confused. "What items are you talking about? What's missing from the lab?"
"Several of the relics." Venna sounded grim. "Including the Mask of Zanta."
Perda gasped. "Really? That's the most powerful relic there is!"
"Yeah. But why would anyone think my parents would want to steal it?" Zann stared at Venna.
"Now that I think about it, you were the one who didn't want the relics destroyed. Why didn't they accuse you?"
Venna frowned at him, looking angry for a second. Then she sighed again.
"Because I have an alibi," she said. "I was in a meeting at the palace when the relics disappeared.
Otherwise, I'd probably be in the dungeon right now too."
"Venna!" a woman called from across the room. "We need you!"
"Coming!" Venna called back. She looked at the kids.
"You four should lie low for the moment," she said quietly.
"I'll get in touch when I figure out how to help the prisoners." She rushed away.
Gliss looked around nervously before pulling the others into the hallway.
"Venna's right," she whispered. "We should get out of here."
Perda didn't seem to hear her. "Who would steal the Mask of Zanta?" she asked.
"And why?" Zann added. "It's such a dangerous relic—the most ancient and powerful one in Magica."
Perda nodded. "At least since the Horn of the Otherworld has been destroyed."
Zann thought back to their last adventure and shuddered.
Morb had stolen the Horn of the Otherworld and used it to give himself an incredible amount of power.
Gliss seemed to be thinking the same thing.
"What if Morb stole the mask?" she said, her eyes widening.
"He might have made it back here to Magica before us."
"He probably did," Perda agreed. "It took us a while, because he stole the guidelink from us."
Zann glanced back into the throne room.
Venna was huddled with Gliss' uncle and several other people. They all looked very serious.
"We should have asked exactly when the relics went missing," he said.
"Maybe we should ask Venna right now."
Darb spoke up. "You heard what she said. She wants us to lie low."
"But we should warn her," Zann said.
"I mean, if Morb really is back, she should know, right?"
"We don't know for sure that Morb is back," Gliss argued. "Maybe he—"
Suddenly a Red popped into view from a nearby doorway.
"Hey!" The man grabbed Gliss by the arm. "What did you kids just say?"
"What?" Gliss tried to yank her arm away, but the man's grip was strong.
"Let go of her!" Zann shouted. "Otherwise we'll call for help!"
Zann was angry, but he was also confused. He had seen this man before. But where?
"Hey, I know you," Darb blurted out. "We saw you at Zann's parents' lab." Darb glanced at his friends. "Remember?"
Now Zann did remember.
The man had been with Venna and the king and queen when they'd whisked his parents away to that important meeting on his birthday.
Zann had thought the man looked familiar back then too.
The man ignored Darb. "I heard you say my brother's name," he said, glaring at Gliss in an accusing way. "Why?"
"Huh?" Gliss blinked in surprise. "What are you talking about?"
"Yeah," Zann added. "Who's your brother?"
The man turned and stared at him. "My brother . . . is Morb."
"What?" Perda cried. She stared at the mysterious man. "Morb is your brother?"
"That's why you look familiar," Zann said. "You look kind of like him."
"What were you saying about my brother?" the man demanded.
Zann's heart pounded. What if Morb's brother was just as evil as Morb?
What if Morb had sent him to capture the kids?
"None of your business," Zann blurted out.
He grabbed Darb with one hand and Gliss with the other, hoping that Perda saw what he was doing. "Zap!"
Splash! They landed in a courtyard fountain just inside one of the palace entrances.
Several guards hurried toward them. "Where did you kids zap from?" the biggest guard demanded.
"The use of magic within palace walls is forbidden without permission!"
Zann stepped out of the fountain. "Since when?"
"Since yesterday." The guard narrowed his eyes. "Who are you anyway? You look familiar."
"Nobody," Zann said quickly. "We were just trying to leave."
The guard snapped his fingers, and the Directory appeared.
A second later he was reading Zann's page. "Oh, I see," the guard said.
"Your parents and grandfather are in the dungeon. Maybe we should take you there as well."
Zann gulped. He tried to figure out how they could escape.
At that moment Morb's brother zapped into view nearby.
"It's all right," he told the guard in a stern voice.
"These rascals slipped away from me, but it won't happen again."
"They're with you, Maff?" The guard sounded surprised.
"Yes. Laddno wishes to speak with them." Maff rubbed his hands together.
Magical shackles appeared around the kids' arms. "Thanks for catching them for me."
"Hey!" Perda cried.
"But . . ." The guard sounded slightly suspicious.
"That will be all, sir." Maff turned away. "Come, all four of you. It's this way."
Zann didn't trust Morb's brother, but he didn't want to end up in the dungeon either.
So he followed Maff out of the courtyard, pulling his friends along.
"Are you sure this is a good idea?" Perda whispered. "What if he's working with his brother?"
Zann wondered the same thing. "Are you really taking us to see Laddno?" he asked Maff.
Maff glanced at him. "Of course not. I hold no loyalty to that bully.
He's as crooked as the Wormwood tree itself."
"What do you mean?" Gliss said. "He's running for King of Magica."
"Yes, and we can only hope that Venna crushes him in the election," Maff said grimly.
"Who knows what Laddno has in mind for Magica if he's elected.
His entire business empire is based on shady deals and black market goods, mostly from other worlds."
"Really?" Perda's eyes widened. "How do you know that?"
"I have my ways," Maff said. "I found out Laddno provided several of the items my brother used in his evil contraptions."
"I thought Wyssa brought Morb all that stuff from other worlds," Zann said.
"She brought most of it," Maff said. "But there were a few things that even she wasn't willing to help Morb with."
"Wow." Zann was stunned. He hadn't paid much attention to Laddno, or worried much about the election either.
But now it sounded as if Laddno was really bad news!
Then again, how could he be sure that Maff was telling the truth? After all, he was Morb's brother.
"If you're not taking us to Laddno, where are you taking us?" Darb asked.
"Wherever the guards won't find you," Maff replied.
"If they dump you in the dungeon, you won't be able to tell me why you were talking about my brother just now."
Zann traded a look with his friends. Perda was frowning.
"We're not going to tell you anything while you're holding us prisoner," she said.
"What?" Maff blinked and then glanced at the magical shackles still holding the kids together.
"Oh, the Shackle spell. Sorry, I only conjured that to trick those guards.
If I release you, will you promise not to zap away again?"
"We won't promise you anything!" Gliss cried.
Maff grinned and snapped his fingers.
Zann braced himself for some horrible new spell to hit them. Instead the shackles disappeared.
Perda rubbed her arm where the shackles had been. "I thought you'd only release us if we talked."
"I'm not my brother," Maff said.
"I hope you'll tell me what I want to know. If not, I'll still help you escape."
"Really?" Perda shot Zann an uncertain glance.
Zann wasn't sure what to say. He was surprised that Maff had released them before getting what he wanted.
That wasn't a very Morb-like thing to do. Maybe Maff wasn't much like his brother after all.
"Come in here." Maff stepped into a nearby room. "We should stay out of sight."
Zann hesitated. Then he shrugged and followed Maff into the room.
"We might as well trust him," he told his friends. "Maybe he can help us free my parents and the others."
"Okay." Perda still sounded uncertain. "So should we tell him about, you know, Morb?"
"Please do," Maff urged. "Then I'll tell you what I know."
"Okay." Zann took a deep breath.
"It started several days ago. I thought I was receiving a Red Share . . ."
He went on to tell Maff the whole story, with his friends chiming in now and then.
Maff looked more and more alarmed. When he heard that Morb seemed to have magic power again, his eyes widened.
And when the kids described how Morb had grabbed the guidelink and disappeared into the vortex, Maff went pale.
"This is terrible!" Maff exclaimed.
"We didn't mean to release Morb," Gliss said.
"He tricked us," Perda added.
"I know." Maff nodded wearily. "You kids shouldn't blame yourselves. This is all my fault!"
"What do you mean?" Perda asked Maff. "How can it be your fault?"
"Yeah, we're the ones who rescued Morb from that houseboat," Zann added.
"But I was the one who created the houseboat," Maff told them.
"What?" Gliss exclaimed. "How?"
Maff sighed. "I didn't want Wyssa to kill my brother," he said.
"I know what Morb did. I know he deserved his fate. But he's my brother." His eyes had a faraway look.
"Maybe if my brothers and sisters and I had been a little nicer to him, things would have been different.
We should have included him more often, even though he was a Void . . ."
Zann glanced at his friends. "Okay," he said. "But how did you stop Wyssa from doing what she planned to do?"
Maff blinked. "Oh. That was easier than I expected. When she left Magica with Morb, I tracked her through the vortex."
"You did?" Perda said. "How?"
Maff shrugged. "I've made a lifelong study of off-world magic," he said. "I used a difficult spell."
Zann nodded. He guessed that Maff was a very powerful Red.
Otherwise he wouldn't be hanging around at the palace with Venna and the other important people in First City.
"I expected the spell to lead me to Fardark," Maff went on. "That's a terrible world where—"
"We know," Zann broke in. "We've been there."
Perda shuddered. "Yes. Wyssa had threatened to feed Morb to a scatter beast."
"I thought that was her plan too," Maff said. "But instead I ended up on Skellia."
"So Ello—I mean Morb—was telling us the truth?" Gliss asked.
"Wyssa brought Morb along when she rescued the Skellian people?"
"Not exactly," Maff said. "Apparently she left him immobilized in an unpopulated world while she transported the Skellians to their new home.
Then she retrieved Morb and brought him to Skellia."
"Why?" Zann asked. "Did she want to feed him to a gulper?"
Maff smiled faintly. "I doubt a gulper would be interested. Morb had no magic left."
"Right," Darb said. "Gulpers eat magic. Morb was back to being a Void."
Maff nodded. "Wyssa had decided that a scatter beast would provide too quick and merciful an end to Morb," he said.
"So she decided to strand him on Skellia. She'd discovered that Morb is terrified of deep water and can't swim."
"Oh!" Now Zann understood Wyssa's plan. "So she left him there with no magic, which means no way to reach a wormhole or navigate the vortex."
"Exactly," Maff confirmed. "There was only a small island left, and the waters were still rising.
She knew that eventually he would drown, but that he'd have plenty of time to ponder his own demise in the meantime."
"Wow, that's horrible," Gliss said. She glanced at the others. "Even for Morb."
"Yeah." Zann shuddered. "So then you found him there?" he asked Maff.
"That's right," Maff said. "He begged me to take him away from Skellia.
I wouldn't do that—he still had to pay for his crimes.
But I couldn't help taking pity on him. I didn't want him to die."
"So you created that houseboat," Zann said.
"Yes. I also provided him with a pair of infused gloves.
They contained just enough self-refreshing magic to allow Morb to create food and other basic necessities."
"Self-refreshing magic?" Perda sounded curious. "What do you mean?"
"It's a very simple type of off-world magic," Maff explained. "It's rather weak though.
That's why I chose it, given Morb's, er, talents for manipulating magic."
"Wow," Gliss said. "Now a bunch of stuff makes a lot more sense."
"But not all of it," Zann added. "Morb only had a weak pair of infused gloves.
So how was he able to do Masking spells and send me weird messages from another world?"
"Good question," Perda said. "Masking spells take a lot of magic energy. At least that's what the books say.
And who knows what kind of spell he used to communicate with Zann."
"I have no idea." Maff shrugged. "I thought I'd considered every possibility, but clearly my brother is even cleverer than I realized.
He must have harnessed some sort of native Skellian magic source to increase the gloves' power."
"Maybe he caught a gulper or something," Perda suggested.
Darb winced. "I hope not," he said. "Or if he did, I hope he treated it better than he did those blue leeches he brought here."
Zann was a little surprised that Darb was so concerned about the gulpers, which were kind of scary.
But Darb did love all animals, from panic bugs to the biggest, nastiest dragons.
"This is looking bad," Gliss declared in a shaky voice. "We have to tell someone that Morb is on the loose!"
"Who can we tell?" Perda said. "First City is in chaos. Nobody even knows where the king and queen have gone!"
"Yeah, and my parents and Boz wouldn't even listen to us," Zann said.
"That is, before they got tossed in the dungeon."
He looked at Maff. "Do you think you could get us in to see them?"
"Are you sure that's a good idea?" Gliss said. "What if the guards throw us in a cell too?"
"It might be worth the risk," Maff said. "Boz and Teplo might have a good idea for stopping Morb."
"You mean you don't know how to stop him?" Perda said.
Maff shook his head and looked grim.
"I'm sorry, I don't. But I'm willing to do whatever it takes if someone else has a plan."
Zann stared at Maff in alarm. If Morb's own brother didn't know how to stop him, what chance did they have?
But he tried not to lose hope. "Okay, let's go to the dungeon," he said.
"We're not supposed to use magic unless absolutely necessary," Maff told Zann and his friends.
"We'd better walk to the dungeon."
"Who banned magic inside the palace?" Zann asked.
"I'm not sure." Maff looked troubled.
The ban sounded strange to Zann. With the king and queen gone, who was in charge at the palace?
Normally it would be the Red Council. But why would they ban magic? It didn't make sense.
A huge guard stood outside the dungeon's entrance.
He wasn't dressed like the other palace guards. His uniform was entirely black.
"Who are you?" Maff asked the guard. "Why are you dressed like that?"
The guard ignored Maff's questions. "What's your business here?" he demanded.
"I want to see my parents," Zann said. "They're in the dungeon."
The guard looked him up and down.
"Go ahead," he said, stepping aside to let them pass. "But don't use any magic."
"That's odd," Maff said as the group walked down the steps.
"That guard wasn't wearing a typical uniform. I wonder what's going on."
Zann spotted more guards below. They were dressed just like the guard upstairs.
Zann pushed past them, eager to see his family.
"Zann!" his father exclaimed. "What are you doing here?"
"We wanted to see you." Zann hurried closer.
His mother was in the cell next to Nax. Boz and Teplo were nearby.
"Uncle Gar!" Gliss cried suddenly. "How did you end up in there?"
Zann quickly scanned the cells. Gliss' uncle was right beside Teplo.
Other members of the Red Council were locked up too.
"I don't see Venna," Perda whispered. She shot a careful glance at the nearest guard.
"Or Saffa," Zann murmured back. "That's good."
The scene reminded Zann of the time when Morb had imprisoned most of the Reds in Magica.
But Morb wasn't doing this, or someone would have seen him.
The thought made Zann feel a little better. But only a little.
How could he talk to his parents and the others with all these guards listening?
Maff seemed to be thinking the same thing.
"May we have a moment of privacy?" he asked the guards.
"The boy wishes to speak with his parents."
"Sorry," a guard said, not sounding sorry at all. "We have our orders. We must stay."
Maff opened his mouth as if to argue. But Zann's mother leaned forward.
"It's all right, kids," Asta said. "It's good to see you, but you don't need to worry about us."
"That's right," Uncle Gar added. "This will all get sorted out after Venna is elected."
"Just stay safe, all right?" Nax said.
Before Zann could answer, footsteps pounded down the stairs.
All the guards spun around and saluted as Laddno stepped into the room.
"At ease, fellows," he told the guards. His hands clasped behind his back, he strolled toward the cells, ignoring Maff and the kids.
"Hello, citizens," he said. "I'm sorry to see you in such dire straits."
"Hmph," Boz said. Nobody else made a sound.
Laddno wandered up and down the row of cells.
"I wish to inform you that your happiness is very important to me," he said.
"If you are all innocent, as you claim, I'll make sure you're released once I've been elected king."
"Why not release them now?" Perda said boldly.
"Nobody seems to be in charge now that the king and queen have disappeared.
I bet you and Venna could join together to free the prisoners right away."
Laddno peered at her. "Who are you?" he asked.
"Never mind her," Boz said. "We're okay, kids. We can wait until after the election."
"Yes," Teplo added. "But if you're worried, you should recite my favorite poem.
It's called 'Ode to a Turnip.'" He cleared his throat.
"Such a fine fruit, ah! Happiness attends the chewing herewith."
Laddno scowled at him. "Enough with the poetry," he snapped.
"I never could stand that nonsense. What's the point of it?"
"What's the point, indeed?" Teplo beamed at him and then winked at Zann.
"Now, be off with you. Children and turnips both require fresh air, hmm?"
Zann exchanged confused looks with his friends.
Teplo had always been a little strange. Had prison finally made his mind snap?
"You heard the man." Laddno gestured to the guards. "Take them outside."
Zann was soon outside the palace walls with his friends.
"Where's Maff?" Perda asked.
"I'm not sure." Zann looked around. The guards had zapped them outside, but Maff was nowhere in sight.
"I guessed he stayed in the palace."
"I've got it!" Darb blurted out.
The others stared at him. "What?" Gliss asked.
"The poem." Darb grinned. "I know what Teplo was trying to tell us."
Zann had already almost forgotten about that silly turnip poem. "What are you talking about?"
"It's an acronym," Darb explained. "The first letters of each word of the poem are S-A-F-F-A-H-A-T-C-H."
Perda gasped. "Saffa hatch!" she exclaimed. "That must mean that Saffa is hiding out in the hatch at Teplo's house."
"She must be afraid she'll be taken prisoner too," Zann said.
"And Teplo wants us to hide with her!" Darb added.
"Shh." Zann glanced around, hoping nobody had heard them. He didn't want to wind up in prison.
"What are we waiting for?" Gliss said. "Let's go!"
All was quiet at Teplo's house. Zann checked to make sure nobody was nearby.
Then he knocked on the hatch outside the front door.
It creaked open, but there was no other sound.
"Should we go down?" Gliss asked, sounding nervous.
"I'll go first." Zann tried to look brave. He sat down on the edge and lowered himself into the darkness below.
Abruptly he let out a scream—his entire body was engulfed in flames!
"Zing, stop that!" a voice cried from the darkness.
A light flared. Gasping in pain, Zann dropped to the floor.
Zing flew around his head, whistling irritably.
"Sorry about that." Saffa hurried forward and touched Zann's arm, instantly healing the burns.
"He's been a little excitable ever since we brought him down here."
"Sorry you got burned, Zann." Teplo's assistant, Fala, stepped into view behind Saffa.
"We zapped your dragon here as soon as we realized you kids had disappeared."
"That's okay. I'm used to getting burned." Zann scratched Zing on the head.
Then he looked up. His friends were peering down anxiously.
"It's okay!" he called. "I'm fine."
Once the others were inside, Fala closed the hatch with a snap of her fingers.
"I'm glad you're here," Saffa told the kids.
She chuckled as Zing snuggled up to Darb. "I think Zing's glad too."
"Thanks." Zann eyed Teplo's sniffer goose, which had just waddled into sight. "Teplo sent us."
"Are the prisoners okay?" Fala asked.
"They seem to be," Gliss said. "My uncle is with them now too."
"Oh dear." Saffa shook her head.
"It seems as if anyone who was close to Boz or Zann's parents is being taken into custody.
Fala and I were afraid we'd be next on the list. That's why we went into hiding.
I'm just glad my husband is traveling far from First City right now."
"Is Venna in the dungeon?" Fala asked.
"No, we didn't see her there," Perda replied.
"Good." Saffa paced around the small room. "Let's hope it stays that way."
"She said she had an alibi for the time when the relics went missing," Zann said.
Saffa nodded. "That may be true. But this situation seems to be about more than the missing relics."
"What do you mean?" Darb asked.
"Who's ordering the guards to take all those prisoners?"
"We have no idea," Fala said. "That's what troubles us the most."
"We might know," Gliss blurted out.
"I hope we're wrong. But we need to tell you something."
"What is it?" Saffa asked.
The kids explained what had happened with Morb.
"Uh-oh," Fala muttered. "This is bad."
"Do you think Morb could be imprisoning Reds again?" Gliss asked.
"I doubt it," Saffa said. "Reds were already being imprisoned before Morb escaped from you."
She started pacing again. "But he's no doubt up to something."
"Yes." Fala sounded grim. "And Magica is extremely weak right now with all the political turmoil.
If Morb shows up, he'll have a good chance of carrying out his evil plans—whatever they are."
"He probably wants to take over Magica again," Perda said.
Gliss shuddered. "Or destroy it!"
Saffa hardly seemed to hear them.
"We need to find out if he's back in Magica yet."
She snapped her fingers, and the Directory appeared. "Morb!" she said.
The Directory showed Morb's page. It hadn't been updated since Wyssa had taken him away several months earlier.
"Hmm." Fala scanned the entry. "That's good. But we shouldn't be too happy.
Morb might have tampered with his entry somehow."
"That sounds like something he'd do," Perda said.
"Maybe he put a Disguising spell on himself so the Directory didn't recognize him when he returned to Magica.
Or maybe he put a spell on the Directory itself, so it couldn't update his entry.
A Dousing spell might work for that."
"If we don't trust the Directory, how can we find out if Morb is here?" Zann said.
"Let's do a Tracking spell." Saffa glanced at Fala.
"Do we have access to anything Morb owned?"
Fala nodded. After digging through a drawer for a moment, she pulled out a ring with a glowing stone.
"What's that?" Zann asked.
"It's from another world. After Morb's first defeat, the Magic Masters searched his lair.
Teplo found this and decided to keep it as a souvenir."
"Perfect," Saffa said. "We can use it as our focusing object."
"Oh, I've read about this kind of Tracking spell!" Perda looked excited.
"If you have an object that belongs to someone, you can use it to draw you toward that person."
"I thought using magic to track other people was illegal." Gliss sounded worried.
"It is," Saffa said. "But this is more important than any law."
Zann nodded. "If Morb is back in Magica, we need to know. Let's do it!"
He and his friends watched while Saffa and Fala prepared the spell, creating a mixture of powders and liquids.
"That looks like one of Wyssa's potions," Perda whispered to Zann.
Soon the potion was ready. Saffa carefully dipped the ring in it.
"Now the ring will pull us toward its owner," Saffa told the kids. "In this case, Morb."
Fala snapped her fingers; the hatch popped open.
Saffa glanced at the kids. "You kids should stay here. It'll be safer."
"No way!" Zann said. "We were the ones who released Morb."
"By accident," Gliss mumbled.
Zann nodded. "By accident. But we still want to help find him."
"And stop him!" Perda added.
Saffa eyed them for a moment and then nodded.
"All right. But let's leave the dragon and the goose here. They'll only attract attention."
"Sorry, little buddy," Zann said as Zing tried to follow them. "You need to stay here."
Once outside, the group walked along, following the pull of the ring.
The object led them out of Teplo's neighborhood, across the river, and along several winding streets. Soon they were in Wormwood.
Fala looked around. "Maybe Morb is here trying to procure some magic items from the locals."
But the ring didn't lead toward any of the huts.
Instead it pulled them straight to the Wormwood wormhole!
"Now what?" Zann stared at the wormhole, which had swirled open at their approach.
"I guess the Directory was right," Darb said. "Morb isn't in Magica."
"Yet." Saffa reminded everyone.
"This could be our chance to find him and stop him before he gets here."
Fala nodded. "We should tell Venna what's going on."
"Good idea," Saffa said.
"But this news is too important to entrust to a message moth. Someone might intercept it."
"You're right," Fala said. "I'll go speak to Venna in person."
She rubbed her hands together and zapped away.
As the others waited, they heard shouts from the area near Wyssa's old hut.
There was a burst of magical energy.
People peeked out from nearby shelters to see what was going on.
Saffa looked uneasy. "I hope nobody starts wondering what we're doing by the wormhole."
Fala reappeared. "Things are getting worse," she said breathlessly.
"I spoke to Venna. She's still safe—for now.
But the guards are looking for you, Saffa."
She turned. "And you too, Zann."
Zann gulped. Then he glanced at Saffa.
"Sounds like it'll be safer for all of us in the vortex. We should go now."
"What about Zing and the goose?" Darb said.
"We can't abandon them in the hatch."
"I'll stay behind with them," Fala said.
"I can use the Remote Eye to keep an eye on things."
Zann remembered the Remote Eye.
It was an old-fashioned magical device that could be used to see long distances.
"Good idea," he said.
Another series of shouts and shrieks rang out from the huts.
"Let's not waste any more time," Saffa said anxiously.
"Be careful." Fala patted Zann on the shoulder and then nodded to the others.
"I'll see you when you return."
She zapped away. Saffa stepped toward the wormhole. "Let's go."
"Wait!" Perda said. "Shouldn't we do a Shackle spell?"
"Why?" Saffa looked confused.
Zann and his friends looked at each other.
"Have you ever been in the vortex before?" Zann asked Saffa.
She shrugged. "I've read about it.
And of course I've discussed it with Nax and Asta and others."
Zann winced. He remembered how overwhelming the vortex was during his first adventure through it.
But then again, Saffa was a Magic Master. Maybe it would be easy for her.
"We always use a Shackle spell in the vortex," Zann explained.
"That way we're sure to stay together."
Once they were shackled, they dived into the wormhole with Saffa leading the way.
"Whoa!" she cried as soon as they were in the vortex.
She waved her arms, which sent the whole group spinning wildly.
"Stop that!" Gliss called. "Just let it pull you along."
"I—I can't!" Saffa sounded breathless and scared.
Zann glanced at his friends. "Maybe we'd better stop for a rest."
Perda nodded.
Zann grabbed the edge of the next wormhole.
The world they were passing looked safe, so he pulled the group through.
After landing on solid ground, he undid the Shackle spell.
Saffa took a few deep breaths and then sat up. She looked around.
"Oh my! Look, there are five suns. This must be Illumos.
Apparently the multiple suns have a multiplying effect on the magic here. Let's try it!"
She rubbed her fingers together.
A second later a hat appeared, followed by several more!
Saffa laughed with delight.
"It's just as Nax and Asta said!" she exclaimed.
"Oh, this is marvelous! I can't believe I'm really here."
She clapped her hands. "I wonder if we could find Chronos next?
I've always wanted to see that world. It sounds so relaxing."
Zann glanced anxiously at his friends. "Shouldn't we focus on finding Morb?"
Saffa's smile faded. "You're right, Zann. Sorry for getting distracted."
"It's okay." Darb grinned.
"We all got kind of distracted our first time visiting new worlds."
After a short rest, Perda redid the Shackle spell.
Saffa handed the glowing ring to Zann.
"Maybe you'd better handle this," she said.
"You have much more experience in the vortex than I do."
"Thanks," Zann said. "But actually, Perda is better with that kind of stuff than I am."
He handed over the ring.
Perda slipped it onto her finger. "Okay, let's go!"
This time Saffa was between Zann and Perda.
That seemed to help her stay calm as they flew through the vortex.
Zann glanced forward at Perda, who was leading the way.
"Is the Tracking spell working?" he called.
"Yes," Perda replied. "It's leading us this way!"
They sped past several wormholes without slowing.
Then Zann felt the ring pulling them toward a wormhole up ahead.
"This must be where Morb is!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Hold on, everyone!" Perda cried.
Zann didn't have time to look at the world before being sucked through the wormhole.
"Oof!" Zann grunted as he landed hard.
Perda stood up and looked at all the trees.
"Whew!" she said. "At least we're not in Fardark."
Zann grinned. "I was thinking the same thing."
"Where are we?" Gliss asked as Perda unshackled everyone.
Zann didn't recognize the world. But he could feel magic energy snapping through the air.
"I recognize those trees from the books," Saffa said.
"I think we're in Atmo."
Zann remembered that his parents had mentioned Atmo.
Suddenly he noticed that Perda was several dozen strides away and moving fast.
"Hey, Perda, wait up!"
"I can't!" she called breathlessly. "The spell is really strong here!"
Everyone rushed after her.
They nearly crashed into her when she abruptly stopped near an enormous tree.
"Careful!" Saffa whispered. "Morb must be nearby."
A cloaked figure stepped out from behind the tree.
"What in all the worlds are you doing here?" an irritated voice asked.
The figure threw back its hood.
Zann gasped. "Wyssa!"
Wyssa glared at Zann and the others.
"I thought I'd seen the last of you when I left Magica."
"We weren't looking for you, Wyssa," Perda said. "This brought us here."
Wyssa's eyes widened when Perda held up the ring. The old woman snatched it away.
"This belonged to my sister," she blurted out.
"She gave it to me as a last gift just before . . ."
Her voice trailed off, and her eyes narrowed. "Where did you get this?"
"The ring is yours?" Saffa said. "We thought it belonged to Morb."
"Ah." Wyssa's expression shifted into a frown.
"I should have known that dirty rat was the one who stole it from me.
He probably planned to use it to blackmail me."
"Oh dear," Saffa said. "If Morb stole the ring from you, it never really belonged to him."
Zann nodded as he figured out what had happened.
"So the Tracking spell worked," he said.
"But it led us to the ring's true owner, not its most recent possessor."
"That makes sense," Perda said. "Otherwise it would have led us to Teplo, because he had it last."
Wyssa held up a hand. "Silence," she said.
"What's going on here? Why are you tracking Morb?
I told you I'd make sure he never bothers Magica again."
Zann bit his lip and flashed a guilty look at his friends.
"Actually, Morb seems to have a new plan."
After he and his friends told Wyssa everything that had happened, the old woman looked furious.
Wyssa whirled away, muttering under her breath, and stomped over to a nearby bush.
She began plucking berries from its branches.
"What are you doing?" Saffa asked.
Instead of answering, Wyssa pointed at Zann. "You, boy," she ordered.
"Go up the lung tree, the one over there with the gray bark.
Break off three twigs from near the top.
Make sure they're small ones, so the tree isn't hurt."
"That's a lung tree?" Zann remembered his parents saying that they'd used a piece of wood from a lung tree to power the infusinator.
"Hurry!" Wyssa shouted.
Zann levitated to the top of the tree.
The air sparked around him, magic energy bouncing off him in ticklish little bursts.
He remembered his parents saying that Atmo's magical energy came from the air.
It felt very strange to be surrounded by that much magic all the time!
When he reached the top of the tree, he broke off the twigs, as Wyssa had requested.
Far below he could hear her barking orders at the others.
Zann glanced down to make sure she wasn't looking up.
Then he broke off another few twigs, which he stuck in his pocket.
Maybe they would help his parents with their experiments, if things ever went back to normal.
"Hurry up, boy!" Wyssa shouted. "What's taking you so long?"
"Coming!" he called quickly and floated back down.
When he reached the ground, Zann saw Wyssa scowl.
She grabbed the twigs out of his hand without saying thank you. But Zann didn't mind.
He was glad that they'd found her, even if it had been an accident.
She might be the only person who could help them find and defeat Morb for good.
Wyssa was crouching down by the pile of stuff she'd been gathering.
Saffa wandered over to look. "Aha!" she exclaimed.
"I just figured out what you're doing, Wyssa.
It's a Locator spell, isn't it? A much more sophisticated one than the one we used though."
Wyssa didn't respond. She was assembling the twigs Zann had brought her into a tepee shape, tying them together with some vines she'd gathered.
"Are you building a contraption like the Secret Eye?" Perda asked.
"Or like those things Morb is always building?" Gliss asked uneasily.
"It does look like Morb's contraptions, only smaller," Zann agreed.
"Where did you learn how to make it?"
Wyssa glanced up. "I need to concentrate," she growled. "Stop your incessant chattering."
The group fell silent while Wyssa continued her work.
Soon the little contraption resembled a pyramid. It was filled with various leaves and stones.
Green berry juice ran down its sides. Finally Wyssa tied the glowing ring onto it.
"The ring is part of the magic?" Saffa asked with interest.
"Will it help you locate Morb because he stole it from you?"
Zann expected Wyssa to ignore that question too. But she glanced up at Saffa.
"No," Wyssa said firmly. "I didn't attach the ring because of Morb.
This ring has been in my family for generations.
That gives me a special connection with it, which will boost the spell's magic power."
"Cool," Perda said. "I've read about that kind of thing. It's sort of like using a relic."
"Silence, please." Wyssa sprinkled a handful of sparkly powder over the contraption.
"Morb!" she intoned loudly. "Show us Morb!"
Zann held his breath as a puff of pale green smoke emerged from the contraption.
It slowly formed into a ghostly image of Morb.
"It's him!" Saffa cried.
Zann stared at the image. It showed Morb standing in a sandy landscape with a jagged ridge behind him.
He was scowling at something Zann couldn't see.
A second later a gust of wind blew the image away.
"Aah!" Gliss cried in frustration. "We didn't see enough to know where he is!"
"Yeah," Zann said. "There must be lots of desert worlds out there."
Wyssa's eyes met Saffa's. "I know exactly where that is," Wyssa said.
Saffa was nodding slowly. "I recognized Dragonjaw Ridge in the background.
It's one of the most recognizable features in the Far Frontier."
"The Far Frontier?" Zann said with a gasp. "But that means . . ."
"Yes," Saffa said grimly. "Morb is already back in Magica."
Wyssa snatched the ring from the contraption she'd built.
"Don't worry," she said. "I'll deal with Morb."
She stomped off, but Zann and the others caught up with her.
"We're coming too," Zann said.
"No." Wyssa shoved him aside.
"It's my responsibility. Now get out of my way."

Zann was relieved. But why had Wyssa changed her mind so abruptly after hearing about the relics?
Before he could ask, he saw a wormhole spinning toward them up ahead.
"Hang on," Wyssa called, yanking them toward it. "We're here."
Zann could tell they'd landed in First City, though he didn't recognize the area.
A light green rain was falling, casting a lime-tinted glow over the whole scene.
"Where are we?" Gliss asked.
"Edgewood," Saffa said, sounding perplexed.
"It's a neighborhood on the far northern border of First City.
But why did you bring us here, Wyssa?"
Zann wondered the same thing.
He realized that it was probably too risky to use the palace wormhole right now.
But why wouldn't Wyssa bring them out in Wormwood?
After all, she used to live there.
"There's no time for idle chitchat."
Wyssa snapped her fingers. "Zap!"
This time Zann recognized the spot where Wyssa had taken them.
"The zoo?" he said, staring at a pair of nibblers in an enclosure nearby.
"Why are we here?"
"Are we going to borrow a dragon to ride to the Far Frontier?" Darb asked.
Gliss glanced toward the dragon pen with a nervous expression.
"The dragons here aren't very tame."
Wyssa didn't seem to be listening.
She peered through the green rain, which was falling harder now.
"My errand here won't take long."
Saffa stepped toward the zoo entrance, looking restless.
"We should check on Venna," she said.
"She might have been taken prisoner by now."
"There's no time for that," Wyssa said.
"We need to find Morb before he gathers more power!"
"The election is less than a month away," Saffa said, sounding stubborn.
"If things get any worse, it could be a disaster for all of Magica."
Zann wasn't too worried about the election.
But Saffa's words had reminded him of his parents.
"We should check on the prisoners too," he said.
"Yes!" Gliss exclaimed. "I want to see my uncle."
Wyssa sighed. "Go," she said. "Make sure they're all okay. I'll wait for you here."
Zann looked at the others. Could they trust Wyssa?
Or would she take off for the Far Frontier on her own as soon as they zapped away?
"Wyssa, we might need your help getting into the palace," Saffa said.
Wyssa didn't look happy. But she agreed to go to the palace with them.
"We have to hurry," she said.
Everyone joined hands. Zap!
They landed at the edge of the palace square.
It was still raining, and Zann had to wipe water from his face before he could see clearly.
When he did, his eyes widened.
The square looked much different than usual.
Dozens of guards were marching around, all of them wearing that new dark uniform they'd seen on the guards in the dungeon.
"What's that all about?" Saffa muttered.
"Who knows?" Perda said.
"Maybe we can figure out a way to sneak in without the guards seeing us."
"We don't have time for that." Saffa sounded impatient.
"This is still Magica, isn't it?
We have the right to visit the palace anytime we like without fearing imprisonment.
I'm tired of sneaking around!"
"But—" Zann began.
It was too late. Saffa was already marching toward the main entrance.
"Should we go with her?" Gliss asked.
"No." Wyssa snapped her fingers, and a glowing wall appeared in front of them.
"Hey." Zann was annoyed. "You can't stop us with a Shield spell."
"It's for your own good," Wyssa said.
Just then Darb poked Zann on the shoulder. "Look!"
Saffa had reached the closest group of guards.
While the kids watched, she appeared to argue with the guards.
A moment later a guard clapped his hands.
A large bubble enclosed Saffa! She yelled and struggled to get out, but it was no use.
The bubble was already floating toward the palace.
"No!" Zann blurted out, louder than he'd meant to.
His voice attracted the attention of a guard.
The guard turned and peered toward them, his face suspicious.
Zann felt panic flash through him.
If they all ended up in the dungeon, there was no way they'd be able to stop Morb!
He grabbed Perda with one hand and Darb with the other. "Zap!" he yelled.
Splash!
They landed in a deep puddle in the gutter outside Teplo's house.
Zann glanced around to make sure his friends were there.
Perda, Gliss, and Darb were there, but someone else wasn't.
"Where's Wyssa?" Perda asked.
"I don't know," Zann said. "I guess she didn't zap with us."
Gliss glanced up and down the street nervously.
"We should get out of sight while we decide how to find her."
Moments later they were in the hatch.
Zing danced around Darb's head, shooting happy flames.
Fala seemed relieved to see them.
"Where's Saffa?" she asked.
"The dungeon, probably." Zann told her what had just happened.
"Oh no!" Fala twisted her hands together.
"This isn't good. Especially given everything that's happened while you were gone."
"What happened?" Perda asked.
"For one thing, the palace guards found the Mask of Zanta in Zann's house."
"What?" Zann cried. "How did it get there? I'm sure my parents didn't steal it!"
"I know they didn't," Fala said. "But now your parents and Boz are in real trouble."
Zann gulped. "What kind of trouble?"
"I'm not sure yet." Fala said.
"They're being kept in the dungeon until the election is over.

"What about my uncle?" Gliss asked. "Did they let him go?"
"No. All the prisoners are staying until after the election," Fala said.
"It's okay," Zann said.
"At least this gives us some time to deal with Morb first.

"Laddno can't do that, can he?"

"Venna wants this to be over, so she didn't object. Neither did anyone else."
"That makes sense," Darb said.
"The longer the campaign goes on, the more time Laddno has to get people all riled up.

"I suppose you're right." Fala looked troubled.
"It doesn't give us nearly as much time to stop Morb though."
"Yeah," Zann said.
"Maybe we should try to rescue my parents before we go to the Far Frontier."
"No," Perda said.
"I'm sure Venna won't let anything bad happen to the prisoners, no matter what happens with the election."
"But—" Zann began.
"Think about it," Perda urged him.
"Morb is a much bigger threat to everyone, including your parents, than anything that might happen with this election.
We have to stop him."
Darb nodded. "Besides, Wyssa won't wait for us if we try to rescue them.

She put it to her eye.
"Check the palace square," Perda suggested.
"That's where we saw her last."
Fala nodded. "I don't see her there," she reported after a moment.
"I'm checking the streets nearby too."
Zann was only half listening. He was still thinking about his parents and Boz.
What if the election took place before Zann and the others returned from the Far Frontier?
And what if Laddno won?
Maff had told the kids that Laddno couldn't be trusted.
What would he decide to do with the prisoners?
Suddenly Zann had an idea.
"Can you use that thing to look inside the palace?" he asked Fala.
She lowered the Eye. "Sure," she said.
"I've been checking on Venna whenever she's there, just in case something strange happens."
"What about the dungeon?" Zann asked.
"Oh, I see." Fala scratched her chin.
"I'm not sure about that. There are probably spells protecting it from spies."
"Can we try?" Zann asked.
"I suppose it wouldn't hurt." Fala raised the Eye again.
After a moment she smiled.
"Hey, it does work! I can see everyone. They all look fine."
She gestured to Zann. "Take a look."
Zann eagerly peered into the Eye.
He gasped as he saw his parents, Boz, Teplo, and the others.
They were talking quietly to one another from their cells.
"I can't believe there are no Shield spells on the dungeon," Gliss said, reaching for the Eye.
"Can I check on my uncle?"
"There probably are spells," Perda said.
"But the Remote Eye is a very old form of magic, remember?
Maybe the spells don't protect against stuff like that."
"That's probably the case," Fala agreed.
"Now let's see if we can locate Wyssa."
The kids took turns scanning the city with the Eye.
Meanwhile Fala tried a few other Search spells, but nothing worked.
"Maybe she really did leave without us," Gliss said.
