over. "Good going, Perda," Darb said. "It looked like Zann and Zing were
both going to get sucked in!" "We were, until Perda grabbed
me," Zann admitted. "Thanks." "Can we get out of this creepy neighborhood now?"
Gliss complained. "There's probably still time for a walk in the park or a boat
ride or something nice like that
before dinnertime." "Soon." Perda glanced at the huge tree. "I want to study
the riddle a little more."
As Zann pushed Zing off him and stood up, he noticed the itchetch creeping closer with its yellow
eyes locked on Zing. The dragon spit a burst of flame at the other
creature. "Stop it, you
two," Zann scolded. "Or if you won't stop, at
least move away from the wormhole." He grabbed Zing's leash and dragged
the little dragon around to the opposite side of the
huge tree trunk. The itchetch followed. Zann released Zing
and looked around. "I've never been to this side of
the Wormwood tree before," he thought. Based on the rocky, rough
ground, he guessed few people wandered here. Several
large roots stuck out of the ground, and Zann noticed that one had a particularly interesting shape. "Come look
at this, you guys!" he called.
Perda appeared a moment later. "What is it?" "Where are Darb and Gliss?" Zann asked, stepping
aside as Zing chased the itchetch past him. Perda rolled her eyes. "I don't
think they heard you," she said. "They're looking for another flower to put in Darb's hair
so the two of them will match." Suddenly Zann couldn't stop wondering what would happen if he tried to put a
flower in Perda's hair. Would she like it, or would
she think it was silly? "What did you want to show
us?" she asked, interrupting his thoughts. "Check out that root." Zann pointed. "Doesn't it
look like an angry troll?" Perda laughed. "Yeah, a little bit!" Then her smile faded,
and she leaned forward. "Wait—do you see something in there?" She pointed to a hole in the root that looked
like the troll's open mouth. Zann hadn't noticed it before, but now
he did. The sunlight shining through the tree's branches glinted off something metallic. "Careful," he said as Perda crouched down
for a closer look. "I heard that the people
in Wormwood sometimes leave stuff for one another near this
tree. Illegal stuff from other worlds, even." "I know." Perda stared into the hole. "But what if it's
not that? The riddle says 'rooted' in
one line, remember? Maybe that's a clue, and whatever's in the
hole is important somehow." Zann wasn't sure about that. It seemed much more likely that the
glinting object was an illicit
stone from another world or something like that. Then again, Perda was one of the smartest people he knew.
Maybe she was right. "Let's try to get it out, then," he
said. "But we should be careful. Don't touch it." Perda
nodded. "Let's try a Levitation spell to lift it out."
She tried the spell on her own first,
but nothing happened. So she and Zann joined their friction by rubbing their hands together. The metal
item didn't move. Perda sat
back on her heels. "We could ask Gliss to help," she said, peering around the trunk.

trying to figure out other spells to use. Or . . ."
She leaned forward and stuck her hand into the hole. Zann bit his

a shock wave of magic energy burst over him. He gasped and Perda's eyes went wide. Even Zing and the itchetch
noticed and stopped chasing each other for a moment. "What was
that?" Zann asked. "It happened right when you pulled your
hand out." Then he gasped again. "Look!" A wormhole suddenly spun open

Perda said. "Is that a
wormhole? It looks . . . different." "I've never
seen one on the ground before," Zann said, taking a step back from the swirling hole.
"And how can it exist
so close to the other one? I thought that never happened." Perda nodded, looking
a bit pale. "Do you think it opened because of this?" She opened her hand to
reveal a small, dirty scrap of
metal. "It looks like a leaf," Zann said. "What if it's a powerful relic, like the
Dragontamer's Charm or something like
that?" Before Perda could answer, they both heard a loud snarl. Zing had
just slapped the itchetch with his tail. The itchetch responded by leaping forward and
giving the dragon a shove. Zing tumbled backward—right into the new wormhole! "Zing!"
Zann shouted, barely managing to grab one of the dragon's wings before it disappeared.
"Oh, no! Not again!" Perda cried, grabbing Zann's arm.
Zann was relieved—but only for a second. Because this time, even though Perda was pulling as hard as
she could, the wormhole kept sucking them farther in. "Help!" he
shouted frantically as his whole arm disappeared after Zing.
"Guys, we need help over here!" There was an answering shout. But Zann barely caught
a glimpse of an alarmed-looking Darb and Gliss.
As they appeared from around the tree, he, Zing, and
Perda were sucked all the way into the wormhole.
Perda knew she should probably be panicking. But she couldn't help being happy about returning
to the vortex. Except . . . this time
the vortex seemed different. It was darker than usual,
with fewer swirling lights. A deafening roar made Perda wish
she could cover her ears. But she was using both hands to
cling onto Zann's arm because they seemed to be tumbling faster
than ever before. "Hold on!" Zann yelled over the noise. "I'll try to grab
a wormhole." Perda looked
around. "Where?" she cried. "There are hardly any wormholes here!" For the first

panic. Normally there were lots of wormholes in the vortex.
The only tricky part was finding the one you wanted—or at least not accidentally pulling

passed by only once every few minutes. "There's one!"
she yelled. "Got it!" Zann had managed to wrap Zing's leash around his waist,
so he used both hands to grab at the edge
of the wormhole. Perda grabbed it too. She saw a steep mountainside covered with dark,
dripping trees. The sky was dark, and jagged flashes of lightning
lit up the scene every few seconds, glaring off
the craggy cliffs overhead. "Weird," she commented. "This wormhole is
in the ground too." "Never mind that," Zann said.
"Are you thinking what I'm thinking?" Perda nodded. "That looks a lot like Fardark," she said with a
shudder. They'd visited the terrifying world a couple of times
and barely escaped alive. It was home to nothing but horrible, violent creatures who

"I never saw
mountains like this in Fardark though," Zann said. "And those trees look like some I've seen in Magica. Maybe

Perda said. "We'll try the next world. But first, let's
make sure we don't lose each other." She rubbed her fingers together to create

himself to Zing as well. They let go and tumbled on through the strange, noisy vortex. For

and Perda halfway through. They paused and looked around. This
time the world before them was rocky and charred,
with almost no foliage. Then there was a screech of fury, and an enormous
purple dragon flew into view. A second, bright
red dragon was pursuing it. It was spitting fireballs as the first
dragon dodged to try to avoid them. The purple dragon
screamed in pain as a
fireball hit it in the back of the head. The dragon spun around and leaped toward the other dragon with deadly claws
extended. The two huge creatures were locked in battle.
They tumbled to the hard ground with a thump that nearly shook loose

servants—and sometimes as food. Zing was peering out through the wormhole. He shot out a
puff of smoke in the direction of the dragons. "That red dragon looks
like a much larger version of Zing," Perda thought. "Maybe it's a type of fire whistler."
She liked Zing just fine, but he could be a little
destructive. That's why Zann was one of the few people in Magica who chose to keep a fire whistler as
a pet. She couldn't even imagine what kind of damage a huge version of Zing could do! "Let's get out of
here before they notice us," Zann said as the
wrestling dragons rolled closer to the wormhole. Once again he and Perda let

to stop and rest soon," Zann said. Perda realized he was right. Already
she could feel the last bits of magic energy ebbing from her
body. That was weird. Traveling through the
vortex always used a lot of energy. But she'd never lost this much energy this

agreed, sounding tired. "At least we already found the two scariest worlds possible." "Not

That world had been full of interesting sights, smells, and people. But
there was no natural magic energy there at all. Perda and
her friends were helpless to do even
the simplest things, like create food or zap from place to place. Plus,
since magic energy was required to open a wormhole, they'd almost been trapped there forever!
"What are the odds we'd end up there again?" Zann said. He grabbed
the next wormhole as it swirled past. Perda
pulled herself up beside him to take a look. "At least the sun
is shining here," Zann said, glancing around. Perda nodded. The land before them was drab and

the boring scene. "This doesn't look like a very exciting world," she said. "But

Zann said. "Let's go!"
Zann realized this wormhole, too, was on the ground. He yanked
on the edge of the wormhole as hard as
he could, propelling himself upward. He flew out and landed
on his feet, but he forgot that Perda was still shackled to him.
"Hey!" she cried. "Whoa!" She crashed into Zann, and the
two of them collapsed on the ground in a tangle
of arms and legs. Zing landed on Zann's face. "Oof!" Zann
grunted, embarrassed to realize that his elbow was in Perda's ear. Perda quickly snapped her
fingers. "Unshackle," she said, undoing the spell. She jumped
to her feet and looked around. "I wonder where we are?"
Zann glanced back just in time to see the wormhole swirl shut and disappear. He
also realized his arm hurt. "Ow," he said, noticing a scrape.
"I think I landed on a rock." He unshackled himself from
Zing. Then he snapped his fingers and touched the wound on his arm to
perform a simple Healing spell. But nothing happened. The scrape still stung, and it still looked red and raw.
"What's wrong?" Perda asked. Zann rubbed
his hands together to create more friction. Then he tried again.
"My Healing spell isn't working!"
he exclaimed. "What if we did land
in that no-magic world again?" "This doesn't look anything like
that world," Perda said. "It's probably not working because the vortex sapped your energy.
You should rest and
then try again in a few minutes." Zann nodded. "I hope she's
right," he thought. "My arm
doesn't hurt that much. But I do not want to be stuck in
a world without magic!" To distract himself, he looked around. The land
was just as flat and colorless as it had appeared from
the vortex. Now that he could see more, though, Zann spotted mountains rising in the distance. He also saw a crooked, weak-looking sapling
growing very close to where the wormhole had been.
It cast only a few jagged slivers of shade that didn't do much to
combat the heat of the blazing sun. "Look over
here." Perda had wandered a short distance away. She was staring down at
some limp greenish gray sprouts. "This looks like
some kind of garden. See? These plants are growing
in rows." "That means there must be people nearby." Zann
noticed a shallow hole in the ground. A crude
stone shovel with a wooden handle was lying next to it.

this hole recently," she said. "See? The dirt on
the shovel is still a little damp, even though the air
here is really dry." Zann was impressed that she'd noticed something like that.
Perda really was one of the smartest people he
knew. She would make a great researcher someday, if that was what she
decided to do for a career. "I wonder where they went," he said. Then he

bushes. "Hey Zing, don't you dare start chasing something! That's what got

undid our Shackle spells after we got here, remember? That means there's at

Magica." Once again Zann was impressed. Before he could respond, Zing yanked on his
leash, which made Zann's arm hurt again. "Ouch," he complained.
"What are you—oh!" A girl stepped into view from behind the shrub Zing

shaking a little. "Where did you come from? One moment I was alone, and then . . ."
Her voice trailed off uncertainly. "I'm Perda, and this is
Zann," Perda said. "What's your name?" "Mellis," the girl replied. "But where

from a world called Magica," Zann said. Mellis blinked in confusion. "You came here from another world?"
"Yes, that's right," Perda said. "Oh." Mellis
looked as if she didn't believe them. But she didn't say so. Instead she said, "Well, wherever you came from, welcome

say there are lots of worlds that haven't been discovered yet," he
said. "I guess we just discovered one." He felt his arm throbbing and lifted

hands on her legs this time. "Heal," she said as she
touched the scrape again. Then she shook her head. "Still nothing—not even when I

together, and then both of them touched Zann's arm. But still the scrape remained, oozing a little bit of blood.

to her. Maybe Perda was right—maybe magic worked
differently here. "Mellis," he
said. "How does magic work here in Terrica?" Mellis blinked in confusion. "Magic?" she echoed. "What's that?"
Perda could see the panic on
Zann's face. She felt a flash of fear
herself. But then she thought again about that
Shackle spell. "It takes magic to reverse that spell,"
she thought. "There must be some magic energy here—at least a little." "Maybe they don't call it magic
here," she said to Zann. "They might use a different word." She turned
to face Mellis. "How do you create things here?
Do you use friction or some other way?" "Friction?" Mellis sounded distracted. "I'm not sure
what you mean. But please, tell me—what is
that creature? I've never seen
anything like it!" She pointed to Zing, who
was sniffing at an insect. "That's
Zing," Zann replied. "He's a dragon. I guess you don't have dragons in Terrica."
Perda shrugged. "Lots of worlds don't have dragons,"

Mellis looked confused again. "You mean, how do I prepare it?"
she asked. "I usually cook
it over a fire, like everyone else. Although my uncle and I grow some

thinking about that Unshackle spell. "I bet this world has

"So you think we're in Wyssa's home
world?" Zann said. Perda shook her head. "This doesn't look like that world at all," she

the image, rubbing one hand on
her leg to create more friction. Finally she felt something land in her other hand. But it didn't feel
like a cup. When she opened her eyes, it didn't
look like a cup either. It was a single airberry, shriveled and dry. "Oh my

just made that berry appear out of
nowhere! You must be nearly as powerful as Zira, the
head of our village council! She can perform incredible feats with

chomped it down eagerly. "Aha! That
must be the only kind of magic here." Zann shrugged. "I guess so.
At least now we know there's some magic energy in this world, even if it's not strong
enough for Healing spells." He glanced at his
scraped arm. Then he gasped. "What is it?" Perda stepped toward him, concerned. "Is your

we go home?" "What's a wormhole?" Mellis asked. But Perda barely
heard her. She and Zann rushed to the
spot where they'd arrived. The dirt and scrubby grass looked the same there as everywhere else.
Luckily Perda remembered that the vortex had
spit them out close to the scraggly
little tree. "This is the
spot," she told Zann. "I'm sure of it." "Back in Magica,
all you have to do to open a wormhole is step close enough to
it," Zann said. "Your own natural magic energy joins with
the energy in the air to open it. So why isn't this one opening?" Perda wiped sweat from her brow

Zann said. "Maybe we have to create more energy to get it to open."
"It's worth a try," Perda agreed.
What Zann had said made sense. Back
in Magica, magic energy was everywhere. Friction was a way of focusing it
to do what you wanted it to do. If the energy here was very
weak, it would probably take much more friction to gather enough magic
energy to open a wormhole. She and Zann spent a few minutes creating as much friction as
they could. Zann got Zing to rub against
his leg to add a little more friction. They even convinced Mellis to help.
"Why are we rubbing our hands together?" she asked at last. "It's a way to

those relics from your parents' lab,"
Perda said. "The reason they're
so powerful is that they're full of superconcentrated magic energy. That
would definitely help us open the wormhole!" Zann flopped down on the
ground to rest. Then he sat up straight. "Hey!" he exclaimed. "What about that weird metal
thing we found in
the Wormwood tree's root? It looked kind of like
a relic. I bet that's what opened the wormhole there. Maybe it will work here too!" Perda
felt a surge of hope. But just as
quickly, her heart sank again. "Maybe," she said. "But I dropped
it when I grabbed you to stop you from falling into
the wormhole. It's still in Magica."
Zann saw Perda's anxious look and felt even more anxious
himself. Mellis stepped closer. "Your arm looks
painful," she said. "The entire village council is meeting at my house today. I can
take you there to see Zira. Her potions will heal
you." "Great! Let's go." Zann whistled for Zing, who flew over. Mellis looked
worried. "Perhaps we should leave your pet behind. Zira is the most
accomplished scientist in this part of Terrica. If
she hasn't seen such a beast before, she might want to study him further." "Mellis doesn't believe we're from
another world," Zann thought. What
if Zira and the other adults felt the same way? Then again, what if they did believe
them? Zira might want to study them too! "We probably shouldn't
mention where we're from," he said to Perda. "We could
tie Zing to that tree to wait for us." Zing let out an angry
whistle and shot a puff of steam in Zann's
face. "That tiny tree? He'd yank it right out of the ground if he doesn't feel like staying," Perda said.
"Maybe we could disguise him
somehow." Mellis looked thoughtful. "He's about the same size as a chupo." "What's a chupo?" Zann asked. "A creature that lives in
the mountains." Mellis pointed toward the mountain range Zann had noticed earlier. "Chupos are

at Zing again. "Everyone has heard of chupos, but few in
this area have seen one. Let's see if we can turn your,
um, dragon into a chupo." First Mellis said they had to hide Zing's gleaming red
scales. She had a bottle of water in
her rough cloth bag, and the kids mixed it with dirt to create
a muddy paste. Zing wasn't happy about having mud rubbed on him. Zann
was glad that he couldn't shoot fire at the moment, only hot
steam. Even so, it was difficult to keep him still. "I wish Darb
were here," he muttered, dodging a slap from Zing's wing. "He can convince Zing
to do almost anything." Perda nodded. "Hold still,
Zing. We missed
a spot." Finally Zing was the same drab color as the landscape.

glanced at Mellis' bag. "Maybe we could wrap him in that," she

rope belt that cinched in her loose
tunic. "We can use this to tie it on
him." Soon Zing was fully disguised. Zann wasn't sure what a chupo looked like. But he
doubted it looked like a dragon covered in mud and draped in a bag.
"Let's hope nobody looks too closely," Mellis said. "It's
the best we can do. Follow me—the farm
is this way." Zing's legs and wings were
restricted by the bag so the kids took turns carrying him. "How
far away is your house?" Zann asked after they'd been walking for
several minutes. "At our current pace, we should be there within an hour," Mellis replied. Zann and Perda traded a dismayed

said. Perda rolled her eyes. "If
we had magic, we wouldn't need better shoes," she reminded him. "We'd
just zap there!" Zann shifted his grip on Zing.
The little dragon felt heavier with every step. Mellis distracted
the visitors by telling them more about herself. She'd lost both her parents to a famine

and now the two of them eked out a living on
their large but arid farm. "It's not easy," she admitted with

I was out there when you
arrived. Uncle Vilkor had sent me to dig a new well." Zann
was amazed by Mellis' tale. Life without magic sounded really difficult! Finally they
spotted a few buildings on the horizon. There was a
small barn, a separate building for storing
dried grains, and a modest one-story house. Three people were sitting
in the yard. By now Zann was so exhausted from the long walk
that he barely took in the names when
Mellis introduced them. Uncle Vilkor was tall and handsome, with a big smile and a strong handshake. "Welcome,

a small, lean woman with steely gray eyes. "Let's
have a look," Zira said, examining Zann's scrape. "Yes, this should be a simple matter. Let's go

quite rare and difficult to make, you know."
She sounded proud of her work. Soon Zann found out why. The moment Zira rubbed her
purple paste-like potion onto his wound,
it stopped hurting. "Wow, thanks!" he said. Then he noticed Krub watching Zing with narrowed eyes. None
of the adults had paid much attention to the dragon
when Mellis had said he
was an injured chupo. But now Zing was nosing at the fire in
the hearth, obviously trying to figure out how to regain his
powers. "What's the chupo doing?" Krub said, sounding suspicious. "Nothing." Mellis grabbed

she was confused. "Where am I?" she thought. Then she
remembered. "Oh yeah. Zann and I are trapped in Terrica." The evening before,
Mellis had taken them to her bedroom, which
contained only a thick mat stuffed with
straw. She and Vilkor had brought in similar straw beds
for Perda and Zann. Perda sat up and yawned. Zann was still asleep. But Mellis was awake. She
was searching the floor in the corners of the room. "What are you looking for?" Perda asked

could answer, the door flew open. "Time to get moving," Vilkor announced. "Mellis, you

her dig the well," Perda told Vilkor. "After all, it was our fault

help dig." "We don't mind." Zann appeared fully awake
by now. He
nudged
Zing with his foot to wake him up. After two helpings of porridge, they started the
long hike to the well site. Zann carried Zing until
they were out of sight of the
farmhouse and then released him from the bag. The girls carried an assortment of

water is scarce in this part of Terrica," Mellis explained. "My uncle

that. I dug next to it instead." Perda shook her head. "It's strange to think how different things

"Wyssa, we might need your help getting into the
palace," Saffa said. Wyssa didn't look happy. But she agreed to go to the palace with them. "We have to
hurry," she said. Everyone joined hands. Zap! They landed at
the edge of the palace square. It was
still raining, and Zann had to wipe water from his face before he
could see clearly. When he did, his eyes widened. The square looked much different than usual. Dozens
of guards were marching around, all of them wearing that new dark uniform they'd seen on the guards in the dungeon.
"What's that all about?" Saffa muttered. "Who knows?" Perda
said. "Maybe we can figure out a way to sneak in without the
guards seeing us." "We don't have time
for that." Saffa sounded impatient. "This is still Magica, isn't it? We
have the right to visit the palace anytime we like without fearing imprisonment. I'm tired of
sneaking around!" "But—" Zann began. It was too
late. Saffa was already marching toward the main entrance. "Should we
go with her?" Gliss asked. "No." Wyssa
snapped her fingers, and a glowing wall appeared in front of
them. "Hey." Zann was annoyed. "You can't stop us with a Shield
spell." "It's for your own good," Wyssa said. Just then Darb poked Zann on the shoulder.
"Look!" Saffa had reached the closest group of guards. While the kids watched, she appeared to argue with the guards. A
moment later a guard clapped his
hands. A large bubble enclosed Saffa! She yelled and struggled to get out, but
it was no use. The bubble was already floating toward the palace. "No!" Zann
blurted out, louder than he'd meant to. His voice attracted the attention of a guard. The guard turned
and peered toward them, his face suspicious. Zann felt panic flash through him.
If they all ended up in
the dungeon, there was no way they'd be able to stop Morb! He grabbed Perda with one hand and Darb
with the other. "Zap!" he yelled. Splash! They landed in a deep puddle
in the gutter outside Teplo's house. Zann glanced around to
make sure his friends were there. Perda, Gliss,
and Darb were there, but someone else wasn't. "Where's Wyssa?" Perda
asked. "I don't know," Zann said. "I guess she didn't zap with us." Gliss glanced up and down
the street nervously. "We should get out of sight while we
decide how to find her." Moments later
they were in the hatch.
Zing danced around Darb's head, shooting happy flames. Fala seemed
relieved to see them. "Where's Saffa?" she asked. "The dungeon, probably." Zann told her what
had just happened. "Oh no!" Fala twisted her hands together. "This isn't
good. Especially given everything that's happened while you
were gone." "What happened?" Perda asked. "For
one thing, the palace guards found the Mask
of Zanta in Zann's house." "What?" Zann cried. "How
did it get there? I'm
sure my parents didn't steal it!" "I know they didn't," Fala said. "But now your
parents and Boz are in real
trouble." Zann gulped. "What kind of trouble?" "I'm not
sure yet." Fala said. "They're being kept in the dungeon until the election
is over. Then the new king or queen can figure out what to do." "What
about my uncle?" Gliss asked. "Did they let him go?" "No. All the prisoners are
staying until after the election," Fala
said. "It's okay," Zann said. "At least
this gives us some time to deal
with Morb first. After all, the election is almost a month away." "No, it's
not," Fala said. "That's another thing that happened while you
were gone. Laddno is insisting on holding the election next week!"
"Let him go!" Perda shouted as Trof yanked Anso's
arm. "Don't tell me what to do!" The plonk farmer
sneered. He grabbed Mellis with his free hand and glared at her. "Did
you bring your friends in to
do your work for you?" "No, of course not!" Mellis cried in terror.
Trof narrowed his eyes. "Zira warned that I'd have to keep an eye on you to make sure you were
working hard enough. It seems she was right. You're the laziest and sneakiest worker I've ever
had! You're lucky I
don't feed you to the plonks." Perda gritted her teeth.
"What do I do now?" she thought. "I can zap out
of here anytime. But I can't leave Mellis and Anso in the hands of this
brute." She was tempted to send a Blast spell at
the farmer. But she held back. For
one thing, it would be difficult to create enough friction for that kind of spell while
shackled. Besides, it wouldn't be right to hurt
him, even though he was holding her friends as prisoners. There had
to be another way to save them. "Please, sir, listen to
me," Perda said. "If you let us go, I can teach you how to use magic." Trof
laughed. "What could a child like you
possibly teach an adult like me?" "I may be young, but I've been doing
magic my whole life," Perda replied. "I come from a world where magic has existed forever.
And the magic here in Terrica seems to
work the same way as it does in my world." "Another world?" The man looked
skeptical. "That's a
very creative story, young lady. But don't expect me to believe it!" "I can't prove that I'm from a different
world. But I'll prove I can do magic. Watch!"
Perda snapped her fingers a couple of times, since she
couldn't rub her hands together while shackled. A
piece of fruit appeared in her hand. "See?" Trof looked surprised, and then suspicious. "Where did that
come from?" he asked. "I was told that only certain people can perform magic. You
must have had that fruit hidden in your clothes or something."
"No, I created it with magic." Perda tossed
the fruit to the plonks. A large
one grabbed it and gobbled it up, snorting happily. The other plonks squealed hungrily. "I
can teach you how to do it too," Perda said.
She quickly created more food, making sure there was enough for all the plonks. Soon the creatures were chomping, chewing,
and grunting with joy. Trof's eyes narrowed. "Are you trying to trick me? If you truly can create
something out of nothing, why not create something more useful? Perhaps a new board to
replace the one the plonks broke yesterday?" He gestured to a cracked section of the rickety wooden fence. "Sure, I can
do that," Perda said. She created more friction, and moments later
a board appeared in front of Trof. His eyes widened. "You did that by snapping your fingers?" "Basically,
yes." Perda briefly explained how friction worked. "Go ahead and try it," she said. "You can create
anything you need—more boards, nails, food . . . anything except humans or animals." Trof still looked suspicious.
But he dropped his hold on Anso, who sidled a
short distance away. Trof didn't notice. He was busy snapping his fingers. "Nails!"
he shouted. Several nails appeared in his hand. He gasped. "It worked! I did magic!" Perda
smiled and nodded. She wished that Trof would let go of Mellis.
Then she could grab her and Anso and zap
them all away. But the farmer was
keeping a tight hold on Mellis' arm, even as he continued snapping with the other hand. He
went on to create a new hat for himself, a hammer to help him fix the fence, and
several more boards. "But wait!" he exclaimed as a
board dropped at his feet. "Why should I waste my time building the fence myself? Can
I make one by magic?" Perda shrugged, still trying to figure out how they could all escape.
"Sure," she said. "You'll need a little more friction for that
though. You could try rubbing both your hands together." She hoped that would make
him drop his hold on Mellis. Instead he
rubbed his free hand vigorously against his
belly. "New fence!" he cried. "Tall and strong, so the plonks can't
break out!" A tall, sturdy fence appeared around the plonk pen. "Very nice." Perda was still
trying to come up
with a plan. "Er, did you say
your worker is sneaky? I can show you how to control her better. I'll demonstrate on this
boy." She pointed at Anso. "Shackle!" Loose shackles appeared on Anso's wrists. "Hey!" he cried. Trof's eyes
lit up. "I bet I can
do that," he
said, turning to Mellis. Perda's heart sank. She'd planned to offer to shackle
Mellis' arms as well, so that Trof would let
go of her. Then Perda could zap the three of
them away and release Anso and Mellis from their shackles once they'd landed. But if
Trof was the one to put a Shackle spell on Mellis, only he could undo it. The
man was already rubbing his hand on
his belly again. "All right,
what was the word you used again?" he asked. Before Perda could figure out
how to respond, there was a loud whistle from
overhead. A second later the new fence burst into flames. Startled, the plonks ran
all around, squealing. Trof cried out in surprise and fear,
and Mellis and Anso both looked scared. But
Perda felt a flash of hope when she looked up and saw
a little, red dragon dive-bombing another section of fence. "Zing!" she cried.
"Zann! You're safe!" Perda rushed into Venna's hideout with Darb
and Teplo behind her. While Teplo talked to Venna and her people, Zann's friends
pulled him aside. "Wow, I'm glad to see you guys," Zann said.
Half an hour had passed since Venna had asked
him to become king, and he was still stunned.
"What's going on?" Perda asked. "That messenger who came to get
us wouldn't tell us anything. Just that he was taking us to you." "Did you find Gliss?" Darb added. "No,"
Zann said. "I never made it to
the zoo." He quickly told them what had happened. Perda gasped. "They want you
to be king?" she exclaimed. "But you're a
kid!" "That's what I said," Zann agreed. "But
Venna said it didn't matter. She said Boz was so popular
here that the people would love
me. And she needs someone who's sure to
be more popular than Slib." "So Slib really
is trying to take over?" said Darb. "That's not all," Zann said. "Yog says he's
pretty sure Slib sent us that password!" "Why would he do that?" asked Perda. "So
we'd go out and get captured by trolls,"
Zann replied. "Especially me and Gliss. Yog
says Slib resents all Reds and thinks we have
too much power." "Kind of like Jev," Darb
said. Zann nodded. "Anyway, Venna doesn't want Slib to take over.
That's why she wants me to volunteer to
be king." "So what did you say?" Perda asked. "At first I
said no way. But now that I've thought about it
. . . " Zann shrugged. "Venna's really powerful and
smart. I figured we might have a better chance of rescuing
Gliss and defeating Morb if we
all work together." "Did Venna say she'd help find Gliss?" Darb
asked. "She promised she'd take care of it as soon as she
made things official," Zann said. "She’s already sent
a messenger to her contacts at the palace
to tell them I'm ready to become king."
He gulped nervously. Was he really ready to be king of Magica?
Just then he noticed that Teplo was frowning as he
talked to Venna. By now two other Reds had arrived. "Maybe we should go see
what they're talking about," Zann suggested. When the kids walked
over, Teplo was speaking. ". . . and I agree that
Boz's grandson could rally the citizens," he said. "But at what cost to
Zann himself? Surely Morb will be on the lookout for him above all others!" "That
may be," Venna said. "But Zann is
brave enough to take on the responsibility. We can keep
him safe if we work together." "Don't underestimate Morb, Venna," Teplo warned.
He turned to Zann. "Listen, my boy.
Think this scheme over carefully." "I have," said Zann. "Venna says she'll help
me rescue Gliss. Then we can work on finding Boz and the others." "That's right,
Zann," Venna said smoothly. Teplo still looked
skeptical. "How do you propose to do
that?" he asked Venna. One of the other Reds spoke up. "This argument
is a waste of time. Zann already said yes. And Slib
is wasting no time trying to solidify his power. We need to show
our candidate to the people of Magica as soon as possible." "I
agree," Venna said. "Sorry, Teplo. I'm afraid you're
outvoted." The old man sputtered with indignation. But
she ignored him, turning to Zann. "It's time to make final preparations. I
want to coach you on what to say when you address the public. And of course we'll
have to do something about your clothes . . ." Zann nodded, feeling overwhelmed.
But he was ready to go along with whatever Venna
said so they could move on to finding Gliss and Boz. Soon he was surrounded
by Venna's assistants. Yog removed Zann's disguise to
reveal his hair and freckles. Others conjured a fresh set of clothes. In the midst of all this, the
door flew open. Before Zann could look to see who had
arrived, he heard a familiar whistle. He spun around. "Zing!" he cried happily
as his dragon flew in just ahead
of Fala. "Surprise!" Perda exclaimed. "We didn't want to tell you in
case it didn't work. But Teplo thought he could
get Zing back." Zann gave the dragon a scratch on the head, ignoring the burn
of Zing's fiery breath on his face. "Good to have you back, little buddy." He looked
around, wanting to thank Teplo. The old man was huddled with Fala.
Both of them looked worried. A
moment later Teplo strode to the center
of the room. "My assistant has brought troubling news," he announced. "She just discovered that the trolls have nearly filled the
dragon pen at the zoo with
prisoners. They intend to zap them all to
Morb's dungeon as soon as they capture one more Red." Zann gasped. "Gliss!" He
rushed over to Venna. "Did you hear that? This
king stuff will have to wait. We've got
to figure out how to rescue Gliss and the
others at the zoo—now!" Venna traded a look with the other
Reds. "I'm sorry, Zann," she said. "Things have already been set in motion.
We must proceed as planned." "But you said you'd help me rescue my
friend!" "I said I'll help you after you become king," Venna
replied. "If we don't act now, Slib will be able
to take power uncontested." "But—" Zann began. Venna interrupted
him. "This is not open for debate. If you're going to become king, it must be now."
Then Teplo spoke up. "Well, Zann," he said quietly, "it seems you have a
decision to make."
Zann pried a rock loose with his shovel. "I assumed they'd
let me stop working when they saw that big piece of crumblestone," he thought
tiredly. Instead Krub and the goon had told him to keep digging. Now they were lounging nearby, sipping from
their flasks. Finally Krub came over to see what Zann was doing. "There's no more crumblestone here," Krub said. "Crawl through to the next chamber
and dig there for a while. We'll
check on you soon, so don't slack off." Zann had to get on his
hands and knees to fit through the
tunnel. But he didn't mind. At least he'd get a break from the two men. The next chamber was long, with a
low ceiling. A short, wiry man was chipping away
at the wall. "Hello." Zann greeted him.
"Do you mind if I dig too?" "Be my guest." The
man peered at him. "Hey, you're the kid I
saw doing magic earlier. You pulled a whole chunk
of stone out of thin air!" "What?" Zann was alarmed. He didn't think
anyone had seen him create the crumblestone. "Don't worry, I won't tell your bosses." The
man leaned closer and lowered his voice. "Especially if you tell me how you did it." Zann was
relieved. "Of course. Magic should be for everyone. I'm happy to teach you." Zann showed the man
how to create friction
by rubbing his hands together. "That's basically all
you need to do. Then you can
create anything, even food. Use a
focusing word to start with. Cookie!" A wiggle root cookie appeared in Zann's hand. The man stared
in awe. "Amazing!" "Now you try it," Zann said with a
smile. "Just think of your
favorite food as you create friction." The man successfully
created a sandwich. Then he made himself new boots.
Finally Zann showed him how to zap from one place
to another. "You're doing great," Zann said as the man zapped from the far end of the cavern back to
where Zann was waiting. "Keep practicing, and soon you'll be
doing all kinds of magic." "Okay," the man
said. "Now show
me how I can punish my enemy." "What?" Zann said, surprised. The man's expression darkened.
"Another miner poached a valuable vein of glowstone from me last week. But he's twice
my size, so I couldn't fight him for it. I want to punish him! How
can I do that with magic?" Zann was alarmed. "That's not how magic is supposed
to be used! The main law in my world is
'do no harm to others.'" The man rolled his eyes. "Your
world sounds boring, kid. That guy harmed me by stealing my vein. Why
shouldn't I harm him back? He deserves it!" Zann
shook his head. "I'm sorry. I can't help you." "Can't,
or won't ?" The man glared at him. "If you won't teach me what
I want to know, maybe I won't keep quiet about
the magic you've been doing. I'm sure your
bosses would love to hear about it." Zann gulped, not sure what to do.
Luckily, at that moment, two other miners entered the chamber. Still, Zann knew he
had to do something to stop the first man from talking to Krub.
"Um, okay," he whispered. "Meet me in the woods by the crooked tree at
midnight, and I'll teach you what you need to know."
For the rest of the day, he couldn't stop thinking about the encounter. What was he going to do? "That
man will be looking for me at
midnight," Zann thought. "And I'll be at the camp, shackled! Maybe Perda and Mellis will arrive before
then. Then we can escape together." But
as night fell, there was
still no sign of his friends. Krub and
the goon camped in the clearing. They invited some
other miners to share their smelly beverage. As the
evening passed, the men drifted off to sleep. Krub forgot to
shackle Zann. "What luck!" Zann
thought with relief. He thought about zapping
back to Vilkor's village. Then he remembered Perda's words again: "Look for other wormholes!"
He glanced into the dark woods. The crooked tree wasn't far away. Was that a wormhole he'd
seen earlier? He decided to find out. "If the others
do show up here, we can escape back to Magica," he thought as he sneaked away. "My parents and Boz can
help us figure out what to do after that." Soon he spotted the crooked
tree looming ahead in the darkness. Seeing it reminded him
of his arrangement with the miner. How long did he
have until midnight? And what would he do if
the man showed up early? The thought made him
nervous. "Just focus on checking for that wormhole," he
told himself. He stepped past the crooked tree into the small clearing beyond. Zann
stepped closer to the shimmer, and a wormhole
swirled open! He stared into the swirling depths with amazement. All he had to do
was step closer, and the wormhole would pull him into the vortex. "Maybe I should go now,
on my own," he thought. "That way I won't have to worry about
the miner or anything else. I can find my way back to Magica
and ask the adults to help save Perda and the others." He took another
step. Then he stopped. He couldn't abandon Zing
or his friends, especially Perda. Besides, she had mentioned that Terrica wasn't in any of
his parents' books. What if he couldn't find his way
back here? The wormhole continued to swirl, almost hypnotizing
Zann. He snapped out of it when someone cleared his throat nearby. It was the
miner. "Hello, kid," he said with a nasty smile. "I'm ready for my lesson now."

episodes.title: A Battle of Wits and Magic

subtitle.text: Perda thought fast. While Zing flew around, sending
blasts of flame everywhere, she snapped
her fingers. "Open," she murmured. The gate in
Trof's new fence burst open. Perda hopped toward a
large plonk and waved her shackled wrists. "Go! Be free!" The plonk spotted the
open gate. With a loud squeal, it raced through. Several other plonks charged after it.
"Hey, get back here!" Trof cried. He ran
after them, finally letting go of Mellis. "Unshackle,"
Perda said to free Anso. "Quick! Grab
Mellis, and then hold onto
me." Anso looked confused. But Mellis was running toward them. "Grab Perda's arm and
hold on tightly!" she said. "Hurry!" Mellis and
Anso held onto Perda, who whistled for Zing. The dragon flew toward her. But Trof
spotted him passing overhead. The farmer reached up and grabbed
the dragon out of the air, slinging him into a
large crate nearby and slamming it shut. Perda gasped. "Zing!" Mellis squeezed her
arm. "Trof is coming! We have to go!" Trof
ran toward them, looking furious. Perda couldn't stand the thought of leaving Zing behind. But if she
hesitated, they would all be trapped again. "Zap!" she cried. When she, Mellis,
and Anso landed, she looked around. She'd
been in such a hurry that she hadn't specified a location. They appeared to have landed back in
the village. "We're near Anso's house," Mellis said,
sounding relieved. She reached over and hugged him. "Go home before you get
into even more trouble because of me." Anso hugged her back, looking uncertain. "Are you sure?" "Yes,
you should go home," Perda said. "Thanks for your help." Anso said good-bye
and disappeared into a house down the street. "Thanks for coming to
rescue me," Mellis said. "Where's Zann?" "I'm not sure," Perda said. "I
didn't even know where Zing was until just now." She bit her lip, feeling worried. "We need
to figure out how to rescue him from Trof.
We also need to find out where Zira
sent Zann." Just then several people hurried into view, talking loudly. "I heard Sir Vilkor
is giving away special golden staffs to
celebrate the creation of his new home!" one
woman exclaimed. A man clapped his hands eagerly. "Let's go—I want one!" "Sir Vilkor
is so generous," another man said. "Life is better, now that he
can bless us with his magical abilities!" Perda scowled
as she listened. How dare Vilkor and Zira keep the secret of magic
to themselves! She was tempted to jump out
of hiding and teach those people to do magic just as she'd done with Trof.
"Wait," Mellis whispered, seeming to guess what she was thinking. "Let's follow
them to this new house they mentioned. Maybe Zann is
there." Perda wondered if she could be right.
Zira had ordered Krub to take Zann to work in a mine. But what if he'd returned? If
they could find him, he could help them rescue
Zing. She and Mellis sneaked along behind the group. They
walked to a huge, fancy mansion near the town square. Mellis looked surprised. "That wasn't there before. My uncle must have built it
in the past couple of days!" "He probably
used up all his magic energy doing so," Perda
said. "Either that, or Zira helped him." She still couldn't believe how powerful Zira seemed
to be. That made it even
more important to make sure Zira didn't keep the secret of magic from the citizens of Terrica.
Nobody should have that much power. "We can worry about that once
we're all together and safe," Perda told herself. "I'm sure we
can come up with a plan to reveal
the truth to everyone." Perda and Mellis hid behind a tree and watched
people lining up in front
of Vilkor's new mansion. "Maybe we should go
inside and ask him to help us," Mellis
whispered. "My uncle isn't a bad
person." Perda wasn't so sure. Vilkor might not be evil, but he was willing to go
along with Zira's evil plan. The only thing he seemed to care about was making his own life nicer. "What if
Zira is in there with him?" Perda whispered. Mellis looked worried. "I
didn't think of that." "I'm not sure we . . ." Perda's voice
trailed off. She'd just felt an invisible tug, as if a
giant hand was pulling her farther down the street.
"Hey, what's going on?" Mellis took several
steps in that direction. "I didn't mean to walk this way!"
Perda gasped, recognizing the feeling. "It feels like a Compel
spell! They're not allowed in Magica." She struggled to stop
herself from moving, but the spell
forced her to follow Mellis. "Let's zap away!" Perda said. "That
might free us from the spell!" Just then two large goons burst
into view. "It's them!" one goon shouted. "Grab them!" Perda lunged
for Mellis, hoping to zap
away. But her shackles prevented her from moving fast enough. The goons grabbed both girls. As
she struggled against her captor,
Perda noticed he had odd purple marks on his face. The
other goon had similar marks. "I can't zap while he's holding me,"
she thought. "Not without taking him with me,
anyway. And I can't leave Mellis behind!" She glanced at the other
girl just in time to see Mellis
snap her fingers. A rock appeared in her hand, and she threw it at the
goon holding Perda. It hit him in
the shoulder. "Ow!" he yelped, letting
go of Perda. "Go, Perda! Zap away!" Mellis shouted. "Save yourself!" Perda
hesitated. She hated to abandon Mellis so soon after freeing her from
Trof. Still, she couldn't help
anyone if she was trapped herself. As the goon reached for her, Perda snapped her fingers. "Zap!"
Zann gulped. "What should I do now?"
he thought. The miner stared at him, his expression eager and cruel. "You
promised to teach me how to get my revenge. Let's get started." Zann didn't
know what to say. Sure, he could teach the man how
to do a basic Immobilization spell. Most kids in
Magica learned that one in case they were ever attacked by a dragon
or other dangerous creature. But Zann couldn't imagine using it on
any human or animal that wasn't threatening his life. It wouldn't be
right. There were other spells the man would probably like too. Nasty, dark spells
that nobody in Magica ever used for
anything. Back in the Old Times,
such spells were common, or so Zann had heard.
But he would never use that type of magic either. "I'm
sorry," he said, shaking his head. "I don't believe in using
magic to hurt people. I won't teach you
to do it." The man rolled his eyes. "Grow
up, kid. The world is a nasty place. I'm just trying to protect
myself. You'll do the same if you know what's good
for you." Was that a threat? Zann wasn't sure, but he didn't like the look
in the man's eyes. "I've made up my mind. I'm sorry. I'd better get back to camp
now." He tried to step past the miner. The
man stopped him with a hand on his
chest. "You're not going anywhere," he
said. "Not until you give me what I want." Zann stepped back. "No," he said as firmly as
he could. "I won't do it." The miner scowled. "Fine. Then I'm going back right now
to wake up your bosses and tell them exactly what you've been doing."
"No!" Zann cried in alarm. "Please don't do that." The man
smirked. "Oh, are
you afraid they'll punish
you? Maybe you'd prefer I punish you myself, huh?" Before Zann could figure out what he meant, the man
ran at him with his fists raised. "Hey!" Zann yelped, leaping out of
the way just in time to avoid being punched.
"Hold still, kid," the miner growled, trying to grab him.
Zann darted away. He was shaking with fear. Nobody
had ever attacked him physically before! "Well, except for
Zing," he thought, with a stab of worry for
his dragon friend. "But that's just playing, at least most of the time." The man
was already coming at him again.
Zann jumped out of the way, which also reminded him of
Zing. Sometimes the easiest way to avoid
the little dragon's attacks was just to jump out
of the way. "Zing hates when I do that
though," he thought as he barely dodged
another blow. "If I don't get out of here
soon, this guy is likely to get even angrier if he can't catch me. And if
he does manage to grab me . . ." Not wanting to think about that, Zann rubbed his hands
together to create enough friction to zap away. As
magic energy sparked from his hands, he was forced to leap aside
to avoid another punch. That brought him close to the wormhole, which swirled open in response to
the friction he was creating. The miner
stopped short, his eyes going wide. "What's that?" Zann stopped to catch his breath, being careful to
stay out of reach. "It's a wormhole," he said. "It leads into the vortex, which connects
all the known worlds." He glanced around at the Terrican landscape. "And some unknown ones too." The man stared into
the swirling wormhole, seeming mesmerized. "Other worlds? What do you mean?" Zann shrugged. "If you promise to stop attacking me, I promise
to tell you all about it." The man turned
and sneered at him. "Oh, another promise from you? Is
this one a lie too? Because it sounds like a tall tale to me. Magic is one thing.
But there's definitely no such thing as a
portal to another world!" He charged
toward Zann, fists raised. Zann didn't have time to completely dodge the attack this time. Instead
he ducked, letting the man's fists pass over his
head. Then he slammed his shoulder into his attacker's torso, hoping to push
